     9	
    10	# Testing and quality
    11	
    12	TaxKit quality depends on deterministic calculation tests, package boundary
    13	tests, graph validation, trace snapshots, API/SDK parity and build/type health.
    14	
    15	## Scope
    16	
    17	This doc owns cross-cutting quality expectations. Detailed rule-package test
    18	requirements live in [Testing and validation](./testing-and-validation.md).
    19	
    20	## Main areas
    21	
    22	- rule-builder unit tests
    23	- ATO golden tests and known scenarios
    24	- property tests for thresholds and monotonicity
    25	- date-boundary tests
    26	- graph validation in CI
    27	- trace snapshots
    28	- package export and browser-safety tests
    29	- API and SDK parity tests
    30	
    31	## Current baseline
    32	
    33	The current repository baseline is canonical root verification:
    34	
    35	```bash
    36	bun run verification
    37	bun run knip:production
    38	bun run test:skills
    39	```
    40	
    41	Root verification includes lint, format, both Knip graphs and workspace type
    42	checks. The development-aware graph covers repository tooling, tests and
    43	current application scaffolds. The production graph separately proves the
    44	eight code-bearing packages in the nine-artifact release closure,
    45	`@taxkit/scripts` exports and commands, and the standalone API runtime without
    46	test or development reachability. It also models the real `apps/docs`,
    47	`@taxkit/docs-content` and `@taxkit/docs-fumadocs` production entries,
    48	including the generated browser/server source consumed by the app and the
    49	build-time Vite/source config. `@taxkit/tsconfig` is JSON-only and remains
    50	covered by strict packed/downstream artifact proof rather than a fabricated
    51	TypeScript entrypoint. Root tools and `apps/web` remain outside the production
    52	graph by ownership. Root verification also typechecks and executes
    53	the root repository-path gate, which scans
    54	Git-tracked readable text and safely reports only repository-relative file,
    55	positive line and closed finding category. Binary files are identified by a
    56	NUL byte or failed strict UTF-8 decode and skipped. For skill governance it
    57	also runs `test:skills`, which validates required policy language and rejects
    58	stale provider-wrapper examples. The root graph also runs
    59	`check:harness-governance` exactly once. That Effect-native gate decodes the
    60	TaxKit profile, structured HE findings/crosswalk, canonical skill receipt, and
    61	critical-journey inventory at filesystem ingress, then checks local skill-tree
    62	digests, the two permitted profile overlays, the two declared extras, eight
    63	relative Claude links, the maintained lifecycle with stable spec/plan index
    64	owners, self-contained references, portable runtime paths, and external
    65	non-claims. Its positive and adversarial corpus is owned by
    66	`tools/governance/`; focused type and test commands are
    67	`check:harness-governance:types` and `test:harness-governance`.
    68	Target-specific requalification is separately owned by
    69	`check:harness-foundation-epoch` and its focused TypeScript check. That command
    70	binds one immutable candidate to complete validator sources, the canonical
    71	skill and journey projections, retained failures, five receipts, fresh
    72	independent review, clocks, limitations and non-claims. It is a closeout check,
    73	not another root-verification or Quality-workflow edge.
    74	For docs, `apps/docs` type checking also
    75	typechecks checked examples,
    76	and dependent package builds run before type checks through Turbo.
    77	`@taxkit/docs-content#generate` names content, navigation, source config,
    78	canonical schema and package-manifest inputs, writes `.source/**`, and follows
    79	the compiled `@taxkit/docs-fumadocs` build. The content build executes that
    80	named generation command, and the docs app build follows both packages.
    81	Heavier
    82	docs runtime gates remain explicit package commands so normal local
    83	verification does not rebuild and validate the whole docs corpus on every
    84	change:
    85	
    86	```bash
    87	bun run docs:validate
    88	bun run docs:build
    89	bun run test:docs-boundaries
    90	bun run --filter=docs test
    91	bun run --filter=docs test:browser
    92	bun run --filter=docs test:built
    93	bun run --filter=docs test:cloudflare-built
    94	bun run --filter=@taxkit/docs-content test
    95	```
    96	
    97	Run those package-local docs gates whenever MDX content, Fumadocs source
    98	wiring, docs examples, validation policy or docs rendering changes.
    99	`test:docs-boundaries` includes a negative browser import audit, the route
   100	transport codec corpus and a focused test that reuses one app-owned server
   101	runtime before the test owner disposes it. The package content test composes
   102	the deterministic `DocsContentService` test Layer over the generic
   103	`FumadocsSource` test Layer and covers accepted, missing and malformed content.
   104	
   105	Release-facing package work must also prove actual tarballs rather than
   106	workspace imports or dry-run file lists:
   107	
   108	```bash
   109	bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk check-packed-artifact
   110	bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk validate:downstream
   111	```
   112	
   113	The focused command uses an Effect-native, scope-managed Bun runtime to pack,
   114	inspect and import the SDK artifact. The strict command builds the nine-package
   115	release closure, materializes each declared dist-only
   116	`publishConfig.exports` view, Bun-packs it, rejects source/protocol leakage,
   117	installs all tarballs in a clean external workspace, typechecks and runs SDK
   118	examples, imports every JavaScript public entrypoint and browser-bundles the
   119	browser-safe SDK surface. It has no audit-only success mode.
   120	
   121	The docs browser command runs a programmatic client-side TanStack route harness
   122	in Chromium. It may prove direct `Route.useLoaderData` restoration, recoverable
   123	route UI, framework error boundaries and console cleanliness, but it does not
   124	prove SSR or hydration. Prove initial SSR, hydration and client navigation
   125	separately against the built app on `https://docs.taxkit.localhost`, including
   126	a successful server-function response and no document request during the client
   127	transition. `bun run --filter=docs test:built` is that built-production HTTP,
   128	workerd and Playwright proof: it serves the generated Cloudflare no-bundle
   129	Worker and static assets on an ephemeral local port, asserts SSR response
   130	content and HTTP 404 before browser inspection, then proves clean hydration,
   131	server-function navigation through real sidebar and authored-MDX links, browser
   132	history, pending and client not-found behavior without another document
   133	request. It also asserts that initial hydration does not steal focus, client
   134	navigation focuses the destination heading, the skip link reaches the main
   135	landmark, navigation is labelled and current, the mobile disclosure is
   136	operable, representative interactive colours meet the owned contrast
   137	threshold, reduced motion removes no required information, immutable asset
   138	headers, runtime reuse and compressed upload limits, and the console is clean.
   139	The command owns workerd/browser cleanup. `test:cloudflare-built` is an
   140	explicit alias. Its screenshot mode is supplemental visual evidence only: a
   141	visually correct image does not prove SSR content, hydration, request resource
   142	type, HTTP status, keyboard or focus behavior, contrast, motion suppression or
   143	console cleanliness.
   144	
   145	The built proof independently builds the official Cloudflare target, verifies
   146	Wrangler's no-bundle dry-run without credentials or bindings, and copies only
   147	`dist/server` and `dist/client` to an isolated temporary directory before
   148	starting Wrangler/workerd. It proves initial SSR, static assets and immutable
   149	cache headers, direct and client not-found behavior, hydration, server-function
   150	transport, no-document client navigation, sequential/concurrent request
   151	isolation, representative accessibility and console/page cleanliness. It also
   152	checks the gzip upload against the 3 MiB Workers Free limit and records local
   153	process-to-first-response and first-response-request timing. Those timings are
   154	readiness observations, not Cloudflare CPU-startup-limit validation. The
   155	provider must establish the account plan, upload acceptance, deployment/runtime
   156	identity and applicable startup-limit readback.
   157	
   158	The separate
   159	`docs/verification/docs-deployment-journeys.json` inventory owns only four
   160	deployment-supporting claims: local workerd, hosted Preview, hosted Production
   161	and Production rollback/operator proof. `bun run check:docs-deployment`
   162	Schema-decodes that owner and the admitted dated receipts. It does not join the
   163	five local release journeys. The accepted DCD-002 requalification chain binds
   164	exact candidate `d9cb8945529fb72158e59ca0daf02a98e1e4de1a`, exact
   165	pre-deploy and pre-destroy state/provider readback, equal plans, provider
   166	Worker/deployment/version/assets/URL readback, hosted HTTP/browser proof,
   167	reviewed desktop/mobile screenshots and exact-stage teardown/absence. It is a
   168	dated Preview-and-teardown observation, not current Preview availability.
   169	
   170	The accepted DCD-003 chain separately validates the first fixed `prod`
   171	deployment, the successor's trusted Preview and exact-stage absence, the
   172	successor Production update, and the normal source-bound redeploy of
   173	`d9cb894…`. Executable cross-receipt checks require two viewport classes,
   174	provider/hosted/screenshot identity equality, distinct deployment/version IDs,
   175	stable Worker/URL/state instance, and restoration of the initial d9 state
   176	bundle. A negative test changes the restored bundle hash and must fail. These
   177	dated observations establish no custom domain, DNS, byte promotion,
   178	known-bad-content recovery, paid-plan or release claim.
   179	
   180	The retained `0d714e6…` observation is disconfirming history: it did not
   181	establish the same pre-mutation, isolate-equality, mobile-request, public-cache,
   182	state-detail or screenshot-input contract.
   183	
   184	The built graph retains Node filesystem code in two qualified, non-normal-route
   185	branches: generated Fumadocs `getText("raw")`, while the runtime adapter calls
   186	`getText("processed")`, and the lazily imported validation policy. The harness

   211	The implemented release-readiness command composes the complete local release
   212	evidence without taking ownership of those validators:

   219	content validation, the focused SDK artifact check, strict downstream package
   220	validation, API smoke, docs browser proof and Changeset status in that order.

   224	implementations remain in their current packages and apps. The live runner

    12	Capability is not authority. Repository access or a runnable command does not
    13	identify the principal permitted to perform a consequential operation. Each
    14	run must bind identity, operation, resource, environment, approval boundary,
    15	duration or revocation, audit receipt, rollback precondition, and escalation.

    18	principal is `unknown`, so their status is `unknown-stop`:

    10	# Controls and automation governance
    11	
    12	The Quality workflow is the executable CI owner for the local release-facing
    13	graph. It has read-only repository permission, a timeout, cancellation
    14	concurrency, an explicit `taxkit-ci-release-maintainer` pin-update owner, and
    15	full-SHA action pins. It invokes `bun run release:check -- --ci` on every
    16	configured pull request and on pushes to `main`; feature-branch pushes are
    17	intentionally covered by the pull-request event rather than running the same
    18	Quality graph a second time. There are deliberately no path filters, so a new
    19	or renamed release boundary cannot be skipped. The preceding bootstrap steps
    20	materialise complete `main` comparison history, resolve cache identities,
    21	perform a frozen Bun install and install Chromium plus its system packages
    22	through the app-local Playwright executable; a shallow checkout, cached
    23	`node_modules`, skipped install or floating browser-tool resolution fails
    24	policy. The Schema-decoded workflow,
    25	control register and negative corpus are owned by `tools/quality-workflow/` and
    26	run through `bun run check:quality-workflow`.
    27	
    28	Every eligible deterministic command under that graph is a Turbo task. Quality
    29	binds the Vercel team cache as read/write on all configured events.
    30	Same-repository pull requests and `main` receive the existing team-scoped
    31	remote-cache token; forks do not. The workflow policy rejects a missing
    32	binding, remote read-only regression, `pull_request_target` and step-level
    33	cache-mode overrides. This
    34	accepts that same-repository pull-request code can access the token. Local cache
    35	writes and the full uncached graph remain available if the credential or
    36	service is absent; cache success cannot replace a command exit status or
    37	release proof.
    38	
    39	Quality separately caches Bun package downloads and Playwright Chromium
    40	binaries through full-SHA GitHub cache restore/save actions. Bun's path comes
    41	from `bun pm cache`; Chromium uses an explicit `ms-playwright` directory under
    42	GitHub's runner temporary directory, outside the checkout. Keys include runner
    43	OS, architecture and `bun.lock`. The Bun key also includes `.bun-version`; the
    44	Chromium key includes the resolved app-local Playwright version. Event name is
    45	excluded so a pull request can restore a matching default-branch cache. GitHub
    46	ref scope keeps pull-request writes away from `main` and sibling pull requests.
    47	Cache operations are non-fatal, saves occur only after the matching install
    48	succeeds, and `bun install --frozen-lockfile` plus Playwright `--with-deps`
    49	always run. A restored Chromium binary does not prove system packages were
    50	installed.

    10	# Docs deployment
    11	
    12	Owner: `taxkit-docs-deployment-operation-owner`
    13	
    14	## Identity and resource scope
    15	
    16	This runbook owns the TaxKit docs deployment made by root `alchemy.run.ts`.
    17	The current graph has one
    18	`Cloudflare.Website.Vite("DocsWebsite")` resource. Alchemy `2.0.0-beta.64`
    19	owns the Vite build, assets, Worker and resource lifecycle.
    20	
    21	Preview uses the exact `pr-N` stage for one same-repository pull request.
    22	Production uses the fixed `prod` stage. The runbook also covers the narrowly
    23	required Alchemy state store and read-only provider checks. It does not cover
    24	custom domains, DNS, unrelated Cloudflare resources, credentials, package
    25	publication or repository releases.
    26	
    27	## Preconditions
    28	
    29	Before an operation, read the current authority model at
    30	`docs/operations/authority-model.md`, the journey register at
    31	`docs/verification/docs-deployment-journeys.json`, and the history router at
    32	`docs/evidence/deployments/README.md`.
    33	
    34	Record these exact values before dispatch:
    35	
    36	- the named person approving the operation;
    37	- `plan`, `deploy`, `destroy` or `rollback`;
    38	- the exact candidate commit and reviewed default-branch workflow commit;
    39	- the pull-request number and `pr-N` stage, or the fixed `prod` stage;
    40	- the expected Cloudflare account and the protected GitHub environment;
    41	- the accepted plan digest and any earlier receipt identity required by the
    42	  workflow;
    43	- the expected postcondition, evidence route and recovery owner.
    44	
    45	The candidate must have a successful Quality result. Preview candidates must
    46	come from the same repository. Use the environment-scoped credential already
    47	attached to `taxkit-docs-preview` or `taxkit-docs-production`; do not copy it
    48	into a local file, command, log or receipt.
    49	
    50	## Authority
    51	
    52	Workflow access is not approval. The named approver must grant the exact
    53	operation, candidate, stage, provider account, protected environment and
    54	expected result. Production also needs the existing protected-environment
    55	review.
    56	
    57	Workflow YAML owns environment selection, GitHub permissions, concurrency,
    58	the provider commands and their order. The typed `workflow-evidence` command
    59	only calculates shared identities, decodes provider output and writes
    60	sanitised evidence. It cannot grant authority or run Alchemy, Wrangler or an
    61	arbitrary command.
    62	
    63	Alchemy login/bootstrap is mutation-capable in beta.64. It may refresh the
    64	provider credential, read a short-lived edge-preview secret, and create or
    65	upgrade state-store resources. Authorise it as part of the exact workflow
    66	operation. Its receipt proves only that the bounded step completed; it does
    67	not prove that no provider state changed.
    68	
    69	The Cloudflare token is available only to the named bootstrap, plan,
    70	replan/apply and destroy steps that need it. It must not be moved to a job,
    71	checkout, install, repository check, hosted proof or artefact upload.
    72	
    73	Production plan, deploy and rollback share the fixed non-cancellable
    74	`taxkit-docs-production-prod` group. Preview deploy and teardown share the
    75	exact non-cancellable `taxkit-docs-preview-pr-N` group. These GitHub locks do
    76	not cover a manual CLI. Do not run a manual Alchemy mutation while the matching
    77	workflow is queued or running. Break-glass manual work needs a separately
    78	authorised sole-writer period and state/provider readback before and after it.
    79	There is intentionally no external lease.
    80	
    81	## Procedure
    82	
    83	1. Confirm the preconditions and run the provider-free repository check
    84	   `bun run check:docs-deployment`. Run the required Quality checks for the
    85	   candidate. Local success does not prove GitHub, Alchemy or Cloudflare state.
    86	2. Dispatch `Docs Preview Deployment` or `Docs Production Deployment` from
    87	   reviewed default-branch workflow code. Supply every exact workflow input.
    88	   Use `operation=plan` first. Do not bypass the protected environment or edit
    89	   the workflow during a run.
    90	
    91	   Use these exact input names:
    92	
    93	   - Preview plan: `operation=plan`, `candidate_sha=<exact trusted PR head>` and
    94	     `pr_number=<positive same-repository PR number>`; leave
    95	     `accepted_plan_sha256` empty.
    96	   - Preview deploy: the same `candidate_sha` and `pr_number`,
    97	     `operation=deploy`, and
    98	     `accepted_plan_sha256=<digest from the accepted Preview plan run>`.
    99	   - Production plan: `operation=plan`,
   100	     `candidate_sha=<exact accepted candidate>`,
   101	     `accepted_preview_commit=<same exact candidate>`,
   102	     `accepted_preview_plan_sha256=<accepted Preview plan digest>`,
   103	     `accepted_preview_run_id=<successful Preview run>`, and
   104	     `accepted_preview_pr_number=<that Preview PR>`; leave
   105	     `accepted_plan_sha256`, `rollback_expected_current_version_id` and
   106	     `rollback_recovery_identity` empty.
   107	   - Production deploy: use the same five candidate/Preview values,
   108	     `operation=deploy`, and
   109	     `accepted_plan_sha256=<digest from the accepted Production plan run>`;
   110	     leave both rollback inputs empty.
   111	   - Production rollback: use the same five candidate/Preview values,
   112	     `operation=rollback`,
   113	     `accepted_plan_sha256=<digest from the accepted rollback plan run>`,
   114	     `rollback_expected_current_version_id=<fresh current Production version>`
   115	     and `rollback_recovery_identity=<identity from the accepted Preview
   116	     provider receipt>`.
   117	
   118	   Do not reuse a plan digest across a changed candidate, stage, lockfile or
   119	   configuration. A placeholder, shortened commit or caller-supplied value
   120	   without its named receipt is not an accepted input.
   121	3. The workflow checks candidate and Quality identity, installs frozen
   122	   dependencies, and runs provider-free docs checks. It then performs the
   123	   authorised bootstrap and runs `alchemy plan`. Alchemy owns the Vite build;
   124	   do not add a second build process.
   125	4. The typed evidence command decodes the raw plan with the single beta.64
   126	   parser. Accept only one `DocsWebsite` `create`, `update` or `noop` action for
   127	   deploy. The plan receipt must bind the exact candidate, lockfile,
   128	   configuration, stage and sanitised plan digest. Stop on another resource,
   129	   another action, malformed output or identity mismatch.
   130	5. Review the plan receipt. For deploy, dispatch the same workflow with the
   131	   exact accepted plan digest. The workflow replans and requires an equal
   132	   digest before apply. It then reads back the exact Alchemy stage, one
   133	   `DocsWebsite` Worker, Cloudflare deployment/version and workers.dev host,
   134	   and runs the hosted HTTP/browser proof.
   135	6. Keep the workflow receipt, provider readback and hosted proof separate.
   136	   Reconcile the completed GitHub run before accepting the receipt. A
   137	   successful source check is not provider proof; provider readback is not
   138	   public-host proof.
   139	7. When a same-repository Preview pull request closes, `Docs Preview Teardown`
   140	   runs from reviewed default-branch code in the same
   141	   `taxkit-docs-preview` environment. It rechecks the closed pull request,
   142	   takes the same `pr-N` lock, compares two destroy plans, destroys only that
   143	   stage, and proves state and Worker absence. An already absent stage is a
   144	   valid no-change result, not an invented delete.
   145	
   146	   The automatic close event supplies the PR and reviewed default-branch
   147	   identity. For a separately authorised manual teardown dispatch, supply
   148	   exactly `pr_number=<closed same-repository PR>` and
   149	   `reviewed_workflow_sha=<current reviewed main commit>`. Do not supply the PR
   150	   head as the workflow SHA.
   151	
   152	The shared Preview environment has no required reviewer, so automatic
   153	pull-request-close cleanup can use the same narrow credential as Preview
   154	deploy. A new receipt is not an open prerequisite for this same-environment
   155	automatic teardown. Require a fresh receipt if the environment, reviewer rule,
   156	credential scope, teardown source binding or lock control changes.
   157	
   158	For integrated local Cloudflare development, use the repository-owned
   159	`docs:dev:cloudflare` script. This is development only. It does not replace the
   160	workflow authority or receipt path.
   161	
   162	## Evidence and postcondition
   163	
   164	Retain sanitised receipts with the exact candidate, workflow run, operation,
   165	stage, account identity, plan digest, provider identity, postcondition and
   166	non-claims. Do not retain a bearer token, temporary secret-bearing URL, raw
   167	profile or machine-local path.
   168	
   169	The current journey definitions live at
   170	`docs/verification/docs-deployment-journeys.json`. Immutable dated provider,
   171	hosted, failure, cancellation, no-op, rollback and teardown records are routed
   172	through `docs/evidence/deployments/README.md`. Use those records as history;
   173	do not copy their old commands into this runbook.
   174	
   175	A deployment is accepted only when the exact workflow receipt, Alchemy stage,
   176	Cloudflare Worker/version and hosted result agree. Teardown is accepted only
   177	when the exact stage and Worker are absent, or when the decoded plan and
   178	readback both prove they were already absent. Preserve failed, cancelled,
   179	superseded and no-op attempts with their limits.
   180	
   181	### Retired history
   182	
   183	Some dated evidence refers to the former `DocsBuild` resource. That name is
   184	history only. It is not a current resource, command, plan expectation or
   185	recovery instruction.
   186	
   187	## Rollback
   188	
   189	For a normal Production rollback, use `Docs Production Deployment` with
   190	`operation=rollback`. Supply the exact accepted recovery candidate, its
   191	accepted Preview receipt identity, the expected current Production version and
   192	the recovery identity required by the workflow. The fixed Production lock and
   193	protected-environment review still apply.
   194	
   195	The workflow must recheck the current version before mutation, plan the exact
   196	candidate, require provider/state agreement, apply through Alchemy and repeat
   197	provider and hosted proof. A source revert or successful workflow alone is not
   198	rollback proof.
   199	
   200	If the current provider version is unknown, Alchemy state differs from
   201	Cloudflare, or the workflow was interrupted during bootstrap, deploy, rollback
   202	or destroy, do not retry. Treat the outcome as unknown. Establish one
   203	authorised writer, read back Alchemy state and Cloudflare inventory, record the
   204	result, then choose a new exact recovery operation.
   205	
   206	## Escalation
   207	
   208	Escalate to the repository owner and deployment operation owner when candidate,
   209	stage, account, plan, state, provider, workflow or hosted identities disagree.
   210	Include the exact run and receipt IDs, the last known safe state, the stopped
   211	step, whether provider mutation may have started, and the proposed read-only
   212	checks. Do not include secrets or raw temporary URLs.
   213	
   214	Ask the protected-environment reviewer to reject the run if the requested
   215	operation is broader than the recorded authority. Ask the Cloudflare account
   216	owner to resolve an account or inventory mismatch. Ask the repository owner to
   217	approve any new workflow, credential scope, lock design or recovery mutation.
   218	
   219	## Stop conditions
   220	
   221	Stop before `versioning`, `commit`, `push`, `tag`, `release`,
   222	`registry-publication`, `deployment`, `provider-access` or
   223	`recovery-mutation` when its named authority is absent or unclear.
   224	
   225	Also stop when any of these occurs:
   226	
   227	- the candidate, workflow, pull request, stage, account or environment differs
   228	  from the approved identity;
   229	- Quality is missing, pending or failed;
   230	- the plan contains another resource, an unsupported action or malformed
   231	  beta.64 output;
   232	- replan differs from the accepted digest;
   233	- Alchemy state and Cloudflare readback disagree;
   234	- a matching manual mutation or workflow is already active;
   235	- a token, secret-bearing URL or machine-local path may have entered evidence;
   236	- bootstrap or provider mutation was interrupted and readback has not resolved
   237	  the outcome.
   238	
   239	## Limitations
   240	
   241	GitHub concurrency does not lock manual CLI mutation or another system. The
   242	repository does not use an external lease. Normal concurrent manual mutation
   243	is unsupported.
   244	
   245	Alchemy beta.64 bootstrap can change provider or state-store data before plan
   246	output. A plan-only workflow is therefore not wholly read-only. Remote and Bun
   247	caches can save time but do not replace frozen installation, live provider
   248	commands or receipt checks.
   249	
   250	The workers.dev readback covers the provider-managed host only. This runbook
   251	does not establish a custom domain. Retained artefacts may expire from GitHub;
   252	the repository fixture manifest keeps only sanitised plan bytes, source
   253	identity and digests, not credentials or full provider responses.
   254	
   255	## Non-claims
   256	
   257	Local checks do not prove a GitHub workflow ran. A GitHub success does not by
   258	itself prove provider state. An Alchemy plan does not authorise apply. Provider
   259	readback does not prove the public site journey. A hosted HTTP response does not
   260	prove DNS or a custom domain.
   261	
   262	This runbook does not authorise Production deploy, rollback, DNS change,
   263	credential creation or rotation, package publication, release, broad
   264	Cloudflare cleanup or unrelated provider mutation. Historical receipts do not
   265	prove current state, and the sanitised beta.64 fixtures prove parser
   266	compatibility only.

    21	`@taxkit/api-http` package with health, generated docs, metadata and public
    22	calculation endpoints, the `@taxkit/calculators` service package,
    23	deterministic core engine primitives, Australian pay, income-tax and STSL rule
    24	packages, a private TypeScript SDK package, private `@taxkit/docs-content`
    25	and `@taxkit/docs-fumadocs` packages, shared testing helpers, shared
    26	TypeScript config, private Effect-native release orchestration and
    27	documentation.
    28

    64	## Core model
    65	
    66	```txt
    67	Schema-branded domain values
    68	  -> Schema.TaggedClass / Data.TaggedClass facts
    69	  -> Context.Tag fact and service providers
    70	  -> Layer.effect rule derivations

    77	layers, parameter layers, dates and policies, it must produce the same output

    10	# Testing and quality
    11	
    12	TaxKit quality depends on deterministic calculation tests, package boundary
    13	tests, graph validation, trace snapshots, API/SDK parity and build/type health.
    14	
    15	## Scope
    16	
    17	This doc owns cross-cutting quality expectations. Detailed rule-package test
    18	requirements live in [Testing and validation](./testing-and-validation.md).
    19	
    20	## Main areas
    21	
    22	- rule-builder unit tests
    23	- ATO golden tests and known scenarios
    24	- property tests for thresholds and monotonicity
    25	- date-boundary tests
    26	- graph validation in CI
    27	- trace snapshots
    28	- package export and browser-safety tests
    29	- API and SDK parity tests
    30	
    31	## Current baseline
    32	
    33	The current repository baseline is canonical root verification:
    34	
    35	```bash
    36	bun run verification
    37	bun run knip:production
    38	bun run test:skills
    39	```
    40	
    41	Root verification includes lint, format, both Knip graphs and workspace type
    42	checks. The development-aware graph covers repository tooling, tests and
    43	current application scaffolds. The production graph separately proves the
    44	eight code-bearing packages in the nine-artifact release closure,
    45	`@taxkit/scripts` exports and commands, and the standalone API runtime without
    46	test or development reachability. It also models the real `apps/docs`,
    47	`@taxkit/docs-content` and `@taxkit/docs-fumadocs` production entries,
    48	including the generated browser/server source consumed by the app and the
    49	build-time Vite/source config. `@taxkit/tsconfig` is JSON-only and remains
    50	covered by strict packed/downstream artifact proof rather than a fabricated
    51	TypeScript entrypoint. Root tools and `apps/web` remain outside the production
    52	graph by ownership. Root verification also typechecks and executes
    53	the root repository-path gate, which scans
    54	Git-tracked readable text and safely reports only repository-relative file,
    55	positive line and closed finding category. Binary files are identified by a
    56	NUL byte or failed strict UTF-8 decode and skipped. For skill governance it
    57	also runs `test:skills`, which validates required policy language and rejects
    58	stale provider-wrapper examples. The root graph also runs
    59	`check:harness-governance` exactly once. That Effect-native gate decodes the
    60	TaxKit profile, structured HE findings/crosswalk, canonical skill receipt, and
    61	critical-journey inventory at filesystem ingress, then checks local skill-tree
    62	digests, the two permitted profile overlays, the two declared extras, eight
    63	relative Claude links, the maintained lifecycle with stable spec/plan index
    64	owners, self-contained references, portable runtime paths, and external
    65	non-claims. Its positive and adversarial corpus is owned by
    66	`tools/governance/`; focused type and test commands are
    67	`check:harness-governance:types` and `test:harness-governance`.
    68	Target-specific requalification is separately owned by
    69	`check:harness-foundation-epoch` and its focused TypeScript check. That command
    70	binds one immutable candidate to complete validator sources, the canonical
    71	skill and journey projections, retained failures, five receipts, fresh
    72	independent review, clocks, limitations and non-claims. It is a closeout check,
    73	not another root-verification or Quality-workflow edge.
    74	For docs, `apps/docs` type checking also
    75	typechecks checked examples,
    76	and dependent package builds run before type checks through Turbo.
    77	`@taxkit/docs-content#generate` names content, navigation, source config,
    78	canonical schema and package-manifest inputs, writes `.source/**`, and follows
    79	the compiled `@taxkit/docs-fumadocs` build. The content build executes that
    80	named generation command, and the docs app build follows both packages.
    81	Heavier
    82	docs runtime gates remain explicit package commands so normal local
    83	verification does not rebuild and validate the whole docs corpus on every
    84	change:
    85	
    86	```bash
    87	bun run docs:validate
    88	bun run docs:build
    89	bun run test:docs-boundaries
    90	bun run --filter=docs test
    91	bun run --filter=docs test:browser
    92	bun run --filter=docs test:built
    93	bun run --filter=docs test:cloudflare-built
    94	bun run --filter=@taxkit/docs-content test
    95	```
    96	
    97	Run those package-local docs gates whenever MDX content, Fumadocs source
    98	wiring, docs examples, validation policy or docs rendering changes.
    99	`test:docs-boundaries` includes a negative browser import audit, the route
   100	transport codec corpus and a focused test that reuses one app-owned server
   101	runtime before the test owner disposes it. The package content test composes
   102	the deterministic `DocsContentService` test Layer over the generic
   103	`FumadocsSource` test Layer and covers accepted, missing and malformed content.
   104	
   105	Release-facing package work must also prove actual tarballs rather than
   106	workspace imports or dry-run file lists:
   107	
   108	```bash
   109	bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk check-packed-artifact
   110	bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk validate:downstream
   111	```
   112	
   113	The focused command uses an Effect-native, scope-managed Bun runtime to pack,
   114	inspect and import the SDK artifact. The strict command builds the nine-package
   115	release closure, materializes each declared dist-only
   116	`publishConfig.exports` view, Bun-packs it, rejects source/protocol leakage,
   117	installs all tarballs in a clean external workspace, typechecks and runs SDK
   118	examples, imports every JavaScript public entrypoint and browser-bundles the
   119	browser-safe SDK surface. It has no audit-only success mode.
   120	
   121	The docs browser command runs a programmatic client-side TanStack route harness
   122	in Chromium. It may prove direct `Route.useLoaderData` restoration, recoverable
   123	route UI, framework error boundaries and console cleanliness, but it does not
   124	prove SSR or hydration. Prove initial SSR, hydration and client navigation
   125	separately against the built app on `https://docs.taxkit.localhost`, including
   126	a successful server-function response and no document request during the client
   127	transition. `bun run --filter=docs test:built` is that built-production HTTP,
   128	workerd and Playwright proof: it serves the generated Cloudflare no-bundle
   129	Worker and static assets on an ephemeral local port, asserts SSR response
   130	content and HTTP 404 before browser inspection, then proves clean hydration,
   131	server-function navigation through real sidebar and authored-MDX links, browser
   132	history, pending and client not-found behavior without another document
   133	request. It also asserts that initial hydration does not steal focus, client
   134	navigation focuses the destination heading, the skip link reaches the main
   135	landmark, navigation is labelled and current, the mobile disclosure is
   136	operable, representative interactive colours meet the owned contrast
   137	threshold, reduced motion removes no required information, immutable asset
   138	headers, runtime reuse and compressed upload limits, and the console is clean.
   139	The command owns workerd/browser cleanup. `test:cloudflare-built` is an
   140	explicit alias. Its screenshot mode is supplemental visual evidence only: a
   141	visually correct image does not prove SSR content, hydration, request resource
   142	type, HTTP status, keyboard or focus behavior, contrast, motion suppression or
   143	console cleanliness.
   144	
   145	The built proof independently builds the official Cloudflare target, verifies
   146	Wrangler's no-bundle dry-run without credentials or bindings, and copies only
   147	`dist/server` and `dist/client` to an isolated temporary directory before
   148	starting Wrangler/workerd. It proves initial SSR, static assets and immutable
   149	cache headers, direct and client not-found behavior, hydration, server-function
   150	transport, no-document client navigation, sequential/concurrent request
   151	isolation, representative accessibility and console/page cleanliness. It also
   152	checks the gzip upload against the 3 MiB Workers Free limit and records local
   153	process-to-first-response and first-response-request timing. Those timings are
   154	readiness observations, not Cloudflare CPU-startup-limit validation. The
   155	provider must establish the account plan, upload acceptance, deployment/runtime
   156	identity and applicable startup-limit readback.
   157	
   158	The separate
   159	`docs/verification/docs-deployment-journeys.json` inventory owns only four
   160	deployment-supporting claims: local workerd, hosted Preview, hosted Production
   161	and Production rollback/operator proof. `bun run check:docs-deployment`
   162	Schema-decodes that owner and the admitted dated receipts. It does not join the
   163	five local release journeys. The accepted DCD-002 requalification chain binds
   164	exact candidate `d9cb8945529fb72158e59ca0daf02a98e1e4de1a`, exact
   165	pre-deploy and pre-destroy state/provider readback, equal plans, provider
   166	Worker/deployment/version/assets/URL readback, hosted HTTP/browser proof,
   167	reviewed desktop/mobile screenshots and exact-stage teardown/absence. It is a
   168	dated Preview-and-teardown observation, not current Preview availability.
   169	
   170	The accepted DCD-003 chain separately validates the first fixed `prod`
   171	deployment, the successor's trusted Preview and exact-stage absence, the
   172	successor Production update, and the normal source-bound redeploy of
   173	`d9cb894…`. Executable cross-receipt checks require two viewport classes,
   174	provider/hosted/screenshot identity equality, distinct deployment/version IDs,
   175	stable Worker/URL/state instance, and restoration of the initial d9 state
   176	bundle. A negative test changes the restored bundle hash and must fail. These
   177	dated observations establish no custom domain, DNS, byte promotion,
   178	known-bad-content recovery, paid-plan or release claim.
   179	
   180	The retained `0d714e6…` observation is disconfirming history: it did not
   181	establish the same pre-mutation, isolate-equality, mobile-request, public-cache,
   182	state-detail or screenshot-input contract.
   183	
   184	The built graph retains Node filesystem code in two qualified, non-normal-route
   185	branches: generated Fumadocs `getText("raw")`, while the runtime adapter calls
   186	`getText("processed")`, and the lazily imported validation policy. The harness
   187	executes normal requests from a temporary working tree containing only emitted
   188	output; it also rejects checkout-absolute paths in the filesystem-bearing
   189	modules. It fails if these branches spread, bindings appear, credential names
   190	enter output, the Worker constructs per request, or output-only execution
   191	fails.
   192	
   193	The Worker entry exposes temporary migration instrumentation only when a
   194	request opts in with `x-taxkit-docs-runtime-proof: construction-count`. The
   195	returned construction count and random isolate identifier contain no
   196	configuration or user data and are not a public API guarantee. This channel is
   197	owned by the deployment migration, reviewed on runtime/entry/privacy changes,
   198	and retired after an equally strong non-public provider oracle exists;
   199	otherwise its bounded carrying cost remains explicit.
   200	
   201	Public API route work should also capture contract evidence from the standalone
   202	API app:
   203	
   204	- generated OpenAPI route evidence from `/api/docs/openapi.json`
   205	- at least one metadata route smoke check
   206	- at least one successful calculation route smoke check
   207	- at least one schema-guided error response with field paths and descriptor
   208	  help
   209	- Changeset status evidence for package-facing changes
   210	
   211	The implemented release-readiness command composes the complete local release
   212	evidence without taking ownership of those validators:
   213	
   214	```bash
   215	bun run release:check
   216	```
   217	
   218	`@taxkit/scripts` runs root verification, workspace tests and builds, docs
   219	content validation, the focused SDK artifact check, strict downstream package
   220	validation, API smoke, docs browser proof and Changeset status in that order.
   221	The command uses the Effect Platform child-process `Command` model through a
   222	`ReleaseCommandRunner` service, records schema-backed outcomes, and fails fast
   223	with tagged execution or non-zero-exit errors. Package-owned command
   224	implementations remain in their current packages and apps. The live runner
   225	depends on `ChildProcessSpawner`; only the Bun runtime entrypoint provides
   226	`BunServices.layer`, and that same runtime resolves the workspace root through
   227	Effect `Path.fromFileUrl`.
   228	
   229	```text
   230	root release:check
   231	  -> @taxkit/scripts runtime
   232	  -> ReleaseCommandRunner
   233	  -> canonical root, app and package commands
   234	  -> schema-backed ordered outcomes or one tagged failure
   235	```
   236	
   237	`release:check` is the complete local release-evidence graph, not publication
   238	approval. Versioning, changelog application and publishing remain explicit
   239	operations after a human reviews pending Changesets and the release impact.
   240	
   241	The Quality workflow invokes `bun run release:check -- --ci` for every
   242	configured pull request and for pushes to `main` rather than relying on path
   243	filters. Feature-branch pushes are covered by the pull-request event, so the
   244	same Quality graph is not run twice for one change. The explicit CI mode runs
   245	the same nine ordered checks without consuming or
   246	rewriting an HGI-203 candidate packet; it returns bounded local command detail
   247	only. The sequential release orchestrator stays live, while every eligible
   248	deterministic root, workspace and app/package leaf runs through Turbo. Root
   249	commands use explicit `//#...:task` entries so a public wrapper never calls
   250	itself. Builds declare their output paths and environment-sensitive inputs;
   251	provider, candidate, receipt, dependency-install and browser-install work
   252	remain live. Its exact read-only runner bootstrap fetches complete Git history,

   254	downloads and Playwright Chromium binaries, then still runs frozen install and
   255	Chromium `--with-deps` through the app-local Playwright executable before the

   258

    10	# TaxKit operational authority
    11	
    12	Capability is not authority. Repository access or a runnable command does not
    13	identify the principal permitted to perform a consequential operation. Each
    14	run must bind identity, operation, resource, environment, approval boundary,
    15	duration or revocation, audit receipt, rollback precondition, and escalation.
    16	
    17	The repository carries no standing authority for the operations below. Their
    18	principal is `unknown`, so their status is `unknown-stop`:
    19	
    20	| Operation | Principal | Status | Required authority receipt |
    21	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
    22	| `versioning` | `unknown` | `unknown-stop` | Named principal; exact package/version train; local checkout; approval scope and duration; before/after manifest receipt; identified revert target. |
    23	| `commit` | `unknown` | `unknown-stop` | Named principal; exact paths, branch and message; approval duration; commit/tree readback; accepted semantic scope and revert owner. |
    24	| `push` | `unknown` | `unknown-stop` | Named principal; remote, branch and expected commit; approval duration; remote SHA readback; prior remote state and recovery authority. |
    25	| `tag` | `unknown` | `unknown-stop` | Named principal; provider, commit and immutable tag; approval duration; provider readback; provider-specific recovery. |
    26	| `release` | `unknown` | `unknown-stop` | Named principal; provider, target commit and hosted release identity; approval duration; release readback; provider-specific recovery. |
    27	| `registry-publication` | `unknown` | `unknown-stop` | Named principal; registry and exact package/version set; credential expiry/revocation; registry readback; deprecation/recovery plan. |
    28	| `deployment` | `unknown` | `unknown-stop` | Named principal; provider-specific app/infrastructure target; environment and duration; provider/runtime readback; tested rollback and reconciliation. |
    29	| `provider-access` | `unknown` | `unknown-stop` | Named principal and identity; exact provider operation/resource/environment; credential duration/revocation; provider receipt; provider-specific recovery. |
    30	| `recovery-mutation` | `unknown` | `unknown-stop` | Named principal; exact recovery target/environment/operation; approval duration; pre/post identity; identified rollback artifacts. |
    31	
    32	Read-only local diagnosis and static validation may proceed within the user's
    33	stated task. When any required field is absent, stop before the operation and
    34	escalate to the requesting repository owner. Never infer authority from prior
    35	runs, tool capability, credentials being present, or evidence that a different
    36	principal acted earlier.
    37	
    38	The exact machine-checked records live in
    39	`tools/documentation/runbook-contract.json`. That sidecar and this table must
    40	agree; neither grants authority. Provider/registry/deployment claims require
    41	current target-system readback by the authorized principal.

    10	# Controls and automation governance
    11	
    12	The Quality workflow is the executable CI owner for the local release-facing
    13	graph. It has read-only repository permission, a timeout, cancellation
    14	concurrency, an explicit `taxkit-ci-release-maintainer` pin-update owner, and
    15	full-SHA action pins. It invokes `bun run release:check -- --ci` on every
    16	configured pull request and on pushes to `main`; feature-branch pushes are
    17	intentionally covered by the pull-request event rather than running the same
    18	Quality graph a second time. There are deliberately no path filters, so a new
    19	or renamed release boundary cannot be skipped. The preceding bootstrap steps
    20	materialise complete `main` comparison history, resolve cache identities,
    21	perform a frozen Bun install and install Chromium plus its system packages
    22	through the app-local Playwright executable; a shallow checkout, cached
    23	`node_modules`, skipped install or floating browser-tool resolution fails
    24	policy. The Schema-decoded workflow,
    25	control register and negative corpus are owned by `tools/quality-workflow/` and
    26	run through `bun run check:quality-workflow`.
    27	
    28	Every eligible deterministic command under that graph is a Turbo task. Quality
    29	binds the Vercel team cache as read/write on all configured events.
    30	Same-repository pull requests and `main` receive the existing team-scoped
    31	remote-cache token; forks do not. The workflow policy rejects a missing
    32	binding, remote read-only regression, `pull_request_target` and step-level
    33	cache-mode overrides. This
    34	accepts that same-repository pull-request code can access the token. Local cache
    35	writes and the full uncached graph remain available if the credential or
    36	service is absent; cache success cannot replace a command exit status or
    37	release proof.
    38	
    39	Quality separately caches Bun package downloads and Playwright Chromium
    40	binaries through full-SHA GitHub cache restore/save actions. Bun's path comes
    41	from `bun pm cache`; Chromium uses an explicit `ms-playwright` directory under
    42	GitHub's runner temporary directory, outside the checkout. Keys include runner
    43	OS, architecture and `bun.lock`. The Bun key also includes `.bun-version`; the
    44	Chromium key includes the resolved app-local Playwright version. Event name is
    45	excluded so a pull request can restore a matching default-branch cache. GitHub
    46	ref scope keeps pull-request writes away from `main` and sibling pull requests.
    47	Cache operations are non-fatal, saves occur only after the matching install
    48	succeeds, and `bun install --frozen-lockfile` plus Playwright `--with-deps`
    49	always run. A restored Chromium binary does not prove system packages were

    16	This runbook owns the TaxKit docs deployment made by root `alchemy.run.ts`.
    17	The current graph has one
    18	`Cloudflare.Website.Vite("DocsWebsite")` resource. Alchemy `2.0.0-beta.64`
    19	owns the Vite build, assets, Worker and resource lifecycle.
    20	
    21	Preview uses the exact `pr-N` stage for one same-repository pull request.
    22	Production uses the fixed `prod` stage. The runbook also covers the narrowly
    23	required Alchemy state store and read-only provider checks. It does not cover
    24	custom domains, DNS, unrelated Cloudflare resources, credentials, package
    25	publication or repository releases.
    26	
    27	## Preconditions
    28	
    29	Before an operation, read the current authority model at
    30	`docs/operations/authority-model.md`, the journey register at
    31	`docs/verification/docs-deployment-journeys.json`, and the history router at
    32	`docs/evidence/deployments/README.md`.
    33	
    34	Record these exact values before dispatch:
    35	
    36	- the named person approving the operation;
    37	- `plan`, `deploy`, `destroy` or `rollback`;
    38	- the exact candidate commit and reviewed default-branch workflow commit;
    39	- the pull-request number and `pr-N` stage, or the fixed `prod` stage;
    40	- the expected Cloudflare account and the protected GitHub environment;
    41	- the accepted plan digest and any earlier receipt identity required by the
    42	  workflow;
    43	- the expected postcondition, evidence route and recovery owner.
    44	
    45	The candidate must have a successful Quality result. Preview candidates must
    46	come from the same repository. Use the environment-scoped credential already
    47	attached to `taxkit-docs-preview` or `taxkit-docs-production`; do not copy it
    48	into a local file, command, log or receipt.
    49	
    50	## Authority
    51	
    52	Workflow access is not approval. The named approver must grant the exact
    53	operation, candidate, stage, provider account, protected environment and
    54	expected result. Production also needs the existing protected-environment
    55	review.
    56	
    57	Workflow YAML owns environment selection, GitHub permissions, concurrency,
    58	the provider commands and their order. The typed `workflow-evidence` command
    59	only calculates shared identities, decodes provider output and writes
    60	sanitised evidence. It cannot grant authority or run Alchemy, Wrangler or an
    61	arbitrary command.
    62	
    63	Alchemy login/bootstrap is mutation-capable in beta.64. It may refresh the
    64	provider credential, read a short-lived edge-preview secret, and create or
    65	upgrade state-store resources. Authorise it as part of the exact workflow
    66	operation. Its receipt proves only that the bounded step completed; it does
    67	not prove that no provider state changed.
    68	
    69	The Cloudflare token is available only to the named bootstrap, plan,
    70	replan/apply and destroy steps that need it. It must not be moved to a job,
    71	checkout, install, repository check, hosted proof or artefact upload.
    72	
    73	Production plan, deploy and rollback share the fixed non-cancellable
    74	`taxkit-docs-production-prod` group. Preview deploy and teardown share the
    75	exact non-cancellable `taxkit-docs-preview-pr-N` group. These GitHub locks do
    76	not cover a manual CLI. Do not run a manual Alchemy mutation while the matching
    77	workflow is queued or running. Break-glass manual work needs a separately
    78	authorised sole-writer period and state/provider readback before and after it.
    79	There is intentionally no external lease.
    80	
    81	## Procedure
    82	
    83	1. Confirm the preconditions and run the provider-free repository check
    84	   `bun run check:docs-deployment`. Run the required Quality checks for the
    85	   candidate. Local success does not prove GitHub, Alchemy or Cloudflare state.
    86	2. Dispatch `Docs Preview Deployment` or `Docs Production Deployment` from
    87	   reviewed default-branch workflow code. Supply every exact workflow input.
    88	   Use `operation=plan` first. Do not bypass the protected environment or edit
    89	   the workflow during a run.
    90	
    91	   Use these exact input names:
    92	
    93	   - Preview plan: `operation=plan`, `candidate_sha=<exact trusted PR head>` and
    94	     `pr_number=<positive same-repository PR number>`; leave
    95	     `accepted_plan_sha256` empty.
    96	   - Preview deploy: the same `candidate_sha` and `pr_number`,
    97	     `operation=deploy`, and
    98	     `accepted_plan_sha256=<digest from the accepted Preview plan run>`.
    99	   - Production plan: `operation=plan`,
   100	     `candidate_sha=<exact accepted candidate>`,
   101	     `accepted_preview_commit=<same exact candidate>`,
   102	     `accepted_preview_plan_sha256=<accepted Preview plan digest>`,
   103	     `accepted_preview_run_id=<successful Preview run>`, and
   104	     `accepted_preview_pr_number=<that Preview PR>`; leave
   105	     `accepted_plan_sha256`, `rollback_expected_current_version_id` and
   106	     `rollback_recovery_identity` empty.
   107	   - Production deploy: use the same five candidate/Preview values,
   108	     `operation=deploy`, and
   109	     `accepted_plan_sha256=<digest from the accepted Production plan run>`;
   110	     leave both rollback inputs empty.
   111	   - Production rollback: use the same five candidate/Preview values,
   112	     `operation=rollback`,
   113	     `accepted_plan_sha256=<digest from the accepted rollback plan run>`,
   114	     `rollback_expected_current_version_id=<fresh current Production version>`
   115	     and `rollback_recovery_identity=<identity from the accepted Preview
   116	     provider receipt>`.
   117	
   118	   Do not reuse a plan digest across a changed candidate, stage, lockfile or
   119	   configuration. A placeholder, shortened commit or caller-supplied value
   120	   without its named receipt is not an accepted input.
   121	3. The workflow checks candidate and Quality identity, installs frozen
   122	   dependencies, and runs provider-free docs checks. It then performs the
   123	   authorised bootstrap and runs `alchemy plan`. Alchemy owns the Vite build;
   124	   do not add a second build process.
   125	4. The typed evidence command decodes the raw plan with the single beta.64
   126	   parser. Accept only one `DocsWebsite` `create`, `update` or `noop` action for
   127	   deploy. The plan receipt must bind the exact candidate, lockfile,
   128	   configuration, stage and sanitised plan digest. Stop on another resource,
   129	   another action, malformed output or identity mismatch.
   130	5. Review the plan receipt. For deploy, dispatch the same workflow with the
   131	   exact accepted plan digest. The workflow replans and requires an equal
   132	   digest before apply. It then reads back the exact Alchemy stage, one
   133	   `DocsWebsite` Worker, Cloudflare deployment/version and workers.dev host,
   134	   and runs the hosted HTTP/browser proof.
   135	6. Keep the workflow receipt, provider readback and hosted proof separate.
   136	   Reconcile the completed GitHub run before accepting the receipt. A
   137	   successful source check is not provider proof; provider readback is not
   138	   public-host proof.
   139	7. When a same-repository Preview pull request closes, `Docs Preview Teardown`
   140	   runs from reviewed default-branch code in the same
   141	   `taxkit-docs-preview` environment. It rechecks the closed pull request,
   142	   takes the same `pr-N` lock, compares two destroy plans, destroys only that
   143	   stage, and proves state and Worker absence. An already absent stage is a
   144	   valid no-change result, not an invented delete.
   145	
   146	   The automatic close event supplies the PR and reviewed default-branch
   147	   identity. For a separately authorised manual teardown dispatch, supply
   148	   exactly `pr_number=<closed same-repository PR>` and
   149	   `reviewed_workflow_sha=<current reviewed main commit>`. Do not supply the PR
   150	   head as the workflow SHA.
   151	
   152	The shared Preview environment has no required reviewer, so automatic
   153	pull-request-close cleanup can use the same narrow credential as Preview
   154	deploy. A new receipt is not an open prerequisite for this same-environment
   155	automatic teardown. Require a fresh receipt if the environment, reviewer rule,
   156	credential scope, teardown source binding or lock control changes.
   157	
   158	For integrated local Cloudflare development, use the repository-owned
   159	`docs:dev:cloudflare` script. This is development only. It does not replace the
   160	workflow authority or receipt path.
   161	
   162	## Evidence and postcondition
   163	
   164	Retain sanitised receipts with the exact candidate, workflow run, operation,
   165	stage, account identity, plan digest, provider identity, postcondition and
   166	non-claims. Do not retain a bearer token, temporary secret-bearing URL, raw
   167	profile or machine-local path.
   168	
   169	The current journey definitions live at
   170	`docs/verification/docs-deployment-journeys.json`. Immutable dated provider,
   171	hosted, failure, cancellation, no-op, rollback and teardown records are routed
   172	through `docs/evidence/deployments/README.md`. Use those records as history;
   173	do not copy their old commands into this runbook.
   174	
   175	A deployment is accepted only when the exact workflow receipt, Alchemy stage,
   176	Cloudflare Worker/version and hosted result agree. Teardown is accepted only
   177	when the exact stage and Worker are absent, or when the decoded plan and
   178	readback both prove they were already absent. Preserve failed, cancelled,
   179	superseded and no-op attempts with their limits.
   180	
   181	### Retired history
   182	
   183	Some dated evidence refers to the former `DocsBuild` resource. That name is
   184	history only. It is not a current resource, command, plan expectation or
   185	recovery instruction.
   186	
   187	## Rollback
   188	
   189	For a normal Production rollback, use `Docs Production Deployment` with
   190	`operation=rollback`. Supply the exact accepted recovery candidate, its
   191	accepted Preview receipt identity, the expected current Production version and
   192	the recovery identity required by the workflow. The fixed Production lock and
   193	protected-environment review still apply.
   194	
   195	The workflow must recheck the current version before mutation, plan the exact
   196	candidate, require provider/state agreement, apply through Alchemy and repeat
   197	provider and hosted proof. A source revert or successful workflow alone is not
   198	rollback proof.
   199	
   200	If the current provider version is unknown, Alchemy state differs from
   201	Cloudflare, or the workflow was interrupted during bootstrap, deploy, rollback
   202	or destroy, do not retry. Treat the outcome as unknown. Establish one
   203	authorised writer, read back Alchemy state and Cloudflare inventory, record the
   204	result, then choose a new exact recovery operation.
   205	
   206	## Escalation
   207	
   208	Escalate to the repository owner and deployment operation owner when candidate,
   209	stage, account, plan, state, provider, workflow or hosted identities disagree.
   210	Include the exact run and receipt IDs, the last known safe state, the stopped
   211	step, whether provider mutation may have started, and the proposed read-only
   212	checks. Do not include secrets or raw temporary URLs.
   213	
   214	Ask the protected-environment reviewer to reject the run if the requested
   215	operation is broader than the recorded authority. Ask the Cloudflare account
   216	owner to resolve an account or inventory mismatch. Ask the repository owner to
   217	approve any new workflow, credential scope, lock design or recovery mutation.
   218	
   219	## Stop conditions
   220	
   221	Stop before `versioning`, `commit`, `push`, `tag`, `release`,
   222	`registry-publication`, `deployment`, `provider-access` or
   223	`recovery-mutation` when its named authority is absent or unclear.
   224	
   225	Also stop when any of these occurs:
   226	
   227	- the candidate, workflow, pull request, stage, account or environment differs
   228	  from the approved identity;
   229	- Quality is missing, pending or failed;
   230	- the plan contains another resource, an unsupported action or malformed
   231	  beta.64 output;
   232	- replan differs from the accepted digest;
   233	- Alchemy state and Cloudflare readback disagree;
   234	- a matching manual mutation or workflow is already active;
   235	- a token, secret-bearing URL or machine-local path may have entered evidence;
   236	- bootstrap or provider mutation was interrupted and readback has not resolved
   237	  the outcome.
   238	
   239	## Limitations
   240	
   241	GitHub concurrency does not lock manual CLI mutation or another system. The
   242	repository does not use an external lease. Normal concurrent manual mutation
   243	is unsupported.
   244	
   245	Alchemy beta.64 bootstrap can change provider or state-store data before plan
   246	output. A plan-only workflow is therefore not wholly read-only. Remote and Bun
   247	caches can save time but do not replace frozen installation, live provider
   248	commands or receipt checks.
   249	
   250	The workers.dev readback covers the provider-managed host only. This runbook
   251	does not establish a custom domain. Retained artefacts may expire from GitHub;
   252	the repository fixture manifest keeps only sanitised plan bytes, source
   253	identity and digests, not credentials or full provider responses.
   254	
   255	## Non-claims
   256	
   257	Local checks do not prove a GitHub workflow ran. A GitHub success does not by
   258	itself prove provider state. An Alchemy plan does not authorise apply. Provider
   259	readback does not prove the public site journey. A hosted HTTP response does not
   260	prove DNS or a custom domain.
   261	
   262	This runbook does not authorise Production deploy, rollback, DNS change,
   263	credential creation or rotation, package publication, release, broad
   264	Cloudflare cleanup or unrelated provider mutation. Historical receipts do not
   265	prove current state, and the sanitised beta.64 fixtures prove parser
   266	compatibility only.

    10	# TaxKit architecture
    11	
    12	This directory is the implementation reference for the TaxKit tax calculator
    13	architecture. It is also the routing guide for the implemented surface that
    14	exists today.
    15	Documentation lifecycle, public/maintainer separation, history, and known owner
    16	gaps are routed by [`../README.md`](../README.md). The legacy
    17	[`../architecture.md`](../architecture.md) path is a tombstone to this file.
    18	
    19	TaxKit is the open-source engine repository. Today it contains a standalone
    20	Bun API app, a TanStack Start web scaffold, a Fumadocs-backed docs app, the
    21	`@taxkit/api-http` package with health, generated docs, metadata and public
    22	calculation endpoints, the `@taxkit/calculators` service package,

    26	TypeScript config, private Effect-native release orchestration and
    27	documentation.

    43	- `packages/docs-content`: private source-only docs contracts, generated

    46	  adapter and render primitive package.
    47	- `packages/core`: deterministic primitives, fact/rule/parameter descriptors,

    49	- `packages/rules/au/pay`: Australian take-home pay and PAYG withholding rule

    10	# Docs deployment
    11	
    12	Owner: `taxkit-docs-deployment-operation-owner`
    13	
    14	## Identity and resource scope
    15	
    16	This runbook owns the TaxKit docs deployment made by root `alchemy.run.ts`.
    17	The current graph has one
    18	`Cloudflare.Website.Vite("DocsWebsite")` resource. Alchemy `2.0.0-beta.64`
    19	owns the Vite build, assets, Worker and resource lifecycle.
    20	
    21	Preview uses the exact `pr-N` stage for one same-repository pull request.
    22	Production uses the fixed `prod` stage. The runbook also covers the narrowly
    23	required Alchemy state store and read-only provider checks. It does not cover
    24	custom domains, DNS, unrelated Cloudflare resources, credentials, package
    25	publication or repository releases.
    26	
    27	## Preconditions
    28	
    29	Before an operation, read the current authority model at
    30	`docs/operations/authority-model.md`, the journey register at
    31	`docs/verification/docs-deployment-journeys.json`, and the history router at
    32	`docs/evidence/deployments/README.md`.
    33	
    34	Record these exact values before dispatch:
    35	
    36	- the named person approving the operation;
    37	- `plan`, `deploy`, `destroy` or `rollback`;
    38	- the exact candidate commit and reviewed default-branch workflow commit;
    39	- the pull-request number and `pr-N` stage, or the fixed `prod` stage;
    40	- the expected Cloudflare account and the protected GitHub environment;
    41	- the accepted plan digest and any earlier receipt identity required by the
    42	  workflow;
    43	- the expected postcondition, evidence route and recovery owner.
    44	
    45	The candidate must have a successful Quality result. Preview candidates must
    46	come from the same repository. Use the environment-scoped credential already
    47	attached to `taxkit-docs-preview` or `taxkit-docs-production`; do not copy it
    48	into a local file, command, log or receipt.
    49	
    50	## Authority
    51	
    52	Workflow access is not approval. The named approver must grant the exact
    53	operation, candidate, stage, provider account, protected environment and
    54	expected result. Production also needs the existing protected-environment
    55	review.
    56	
    57	Workflow YAML owns environment selection, GitHub permissions, concurrency,
    58	the provider commands and their order. The typed `workflow-evidence` command
    59	only calculates shared identities, decodes provider output and writes
    60	sanitised evidence. It cannot grant authority or run Alchemy, Wrangler or an
    61	arbitrary command.
    62	
    63	Alchemy login/bootstrap is mutation-capable in beta.64. It may refresh the
    64	provider credential, read a short-lived edge-preview secret, and create or
    65	upgrade state-store resources. Authorise it as part of the exact workflow
    66	operation. Its receipt proves only that the bounded step completed; it does
    67	not prove that no provider state changed.
    68	
    69	The Cloudflare token is available only to the named bootstrap, plan,
    70	replan/apply and destroy steps that need it. It must not be moved to a job,
    71	checkout, install, repository check, hosted proof or artefact upload.
    72	
    73	Production plan, deploy and rollback share the fixed non-cancellable
    74	`taxkit-docs-production-prod` group. Preview deploy and teardown share the
    75	exact non-cancellable `taxkit-docs-preview-pr-N` group. These GitHub locks do
    76	not cover a manual CLI. Do not run a manual Alchemy mutation while the matching
    77	workflow is queued or running. Break-glass manual work needs a separately
    78	authorised sole-writer period and state/provider readback before and after it.
    79	There is intentionally no external lease.
    80	
    81	## Procedure
    82	
    83	1. Confirm the preconditions and run the provider-free repository check
    84	   `bun run check:docs-deployment`. Run the required Quality checks for the
    85	   candidate. Local success does not prove GitHub, Alchemy or Cloudflare state.
    86	2. Dispatch `Docs Preview Deployment` or `Docs Production Deployment` from
    87	   reviewed default-branch workflow code. Supply every exact workflow input.
    88	   Use `operation=plan` first. Do not bypass the protected environment or edit
    89	   the workflow during a run.
    90	
    91	   Use these exact input names:
    92	
    93	   - Preview plan: `operation=plan`, `candidate_sha=<exact trusted PR head>` and
    94	     `pr_number=<positive same-repository PR number>`; leave
    95	     `accepted_plan_sha256` empty.
    96	   - Preview deploy: the same `candidate_sha` and `pr_number`,
    97	     `operation=deploy`, and
    98	     `accepted_plan_sha256=<digest from the accepted Preview plan run>`.
    99	   - Production plan: `operation=plan`,
   100	     `candidate_sha=<exact accepted candidate>`,
   101	     `accepted_preview_commit=<same exact candidate>`,
   102	     `accepted_preview_plan_sha256=<accepted Preview plan digest>`,
   103	     `accepted_preview_run_id=<successful Preview run>`, and
   104	     `accepted_preview_pr_number=<that Preview PR>`; leave
   105	     `accepted_plan_sha256`, `rollback_expected_current_version_id` and
   106	     `rollback_recovery_identity` empty.
   107	   - Production deploy: use the same five candidate/Preview values,
   108	     `operation=deploy`, and
   109	     `accepted_plan_sha256=<digest from the accepted Production plan run>`;
   110	     leave both rollback inputs empty.
   111	   - Production rollback: use the same five candidate/Preview values,
   112	     `operation=rollback`,
   113	     `accepted_plan_sha256=<digest from the accepted rollback plan run>`,
   114	     `rollback_expected_current_version_id=<fresh current Production version>`
   115	     and `rollback_recovery_identity=<identity from the accepted Preview
   116	     provider receipt>`.
   117	
   118	   Do not reuse a plan digest across a changed candidate, stage, lockfile or
   119	   configuration. A placeholder, shortened commit or caller-supplied value
   120	   without its named receipt is not an accepted input.
   121	3. The workflow checks candidate and Quality identity, installs frozen
   122	   dependencies, and runs provider-free docs checks. It then performs the
   123	   authorised bootstrap and runs `alchemy plan`. Alchemy owns the Vite build;
   124	   do not add a second build process.
   125	4. The typed evidence command decodes the raw plan with the single beta.64
   126	   parser. Accept only one `DocsWebsite` `create`, `update` or `noop` action for
   127	   deploy. The plan receipt must bind the exact candidate, lockfile,
   128	   configuration, stage and sanitised plan digest. Stop on another resource,
   129	   another action, malformed output or identity mismatch.
   130	5. Review the plan receipt. For deploy, dispatch the same workflow with the
   131	   exact accepted plan digest. The workflow replans and requires an equal
   132	   digest before apply. It then reads back the exact Alchemy stage, one
   133	   `DocsWebsite` Worker, Cloudflare deployment/version and workers.dev host,
   134	   and runs the hosted HTTP/browser proof.
   135	6. Keep the workflow receipt, provider readback and hosted proof separate.
   136	   Reconcile the completed GitHub run before accepting the receipt. A
   137	   successful source check is not provider proof; provider readback is not
   138	   public-host proof.
   139	7. When a same-repository Preview pull request closes, `Docs Preview Teardown`
   140	   runs from reviewed default-branch code in the same
   141	   `taxkit-docs-preview` environment. It rechecks the closed pull request,
   142	   takes the same `pr-N` lock, compares two destroy plans, destroys only that
   143	   stage, and proves state and Worker absence. An already absent stage is a
   144	   valid no-change result, not an invented delete.
   145	
   146	   The automatic close event supplies the PR and reviewed default-branch
   147	   identity. For a separately authorised manual teardown dispatch, supply
   148	   exactly `pr_number=<closed same-repository PR>` and
   149	   `reviewed_workflow_sha=<current reviewed main commit>`. Do not supply the PR
   150	   head as the workflow SHA.
