   152	The shared Preview environment has no required reviewer, so automatic
   153	pull-request-close cleanup can use the same narrow credential as Preview
   154	deploy. A new receipt is not an open prerequisite for this same-environment
   155	automatic teardown. Require a fresh receipt if the environment, reviewer rule,
   156	credential scope, teardown source binding or lock control changes.
   157	
   158	For integrated local Cloudflare development, use the repository-owned
   159	`docs:dev:cloudflare` script. This is development only. It does not replace the
   160	workflow authority or receipt path.
   161	
   162	## Evidence and postcondition
   163	
   164	Retain sanitised receipts with the exact candidate, workflow run, operation,
   165	stage, account identity, plan digest, provider identity, postcondition and
   166	non-claims. Do not retain a bearer token, temporary secret-bearing URL, raw
   167	profile or machine-local path.
   168	
   169	The current journey definitions live at
   170	`docs/verification/docs-deployment-journeys.json`. Immutable dated provider,
   171	hosted, failure, cancellation, no-op, rollback and teardown records are routed
   172	through `docs/evidence/deployments/README.md`. Use those records as history;
   173	do not copy their old commands into this runbook.
   174	
   175	A deployment is accepted only when the exact workflow receipt, Alchemy stage,
   176	Cloudflare Worker/version and hosted result agree. Teardown is accepted only
   177	when the exact stage and Worker are absent, or when the decoded plan and
   178	readback both prove they were already absent. Preserve failed, cancelled,
   179	superseded and no-op attempts with their limits.
   180	
   181	### Retired history
   182	
   183	Some dated evidence refers to the former `DocsBuild` resource. That name is
   184	history only. It is not a current resource, command, plan expectation or
   185	recovery instruction.
   186	
   187	## Rollback
   188	
   189	For a normal Production rollback, use `Docs Production Deployment` with
   190	`operation=rollback`. Supply the exact accepted recovery candidate, its
   191	accepted Preview receipt identity, the expected current Production version and
   192	the recovery identity required by the workflow. The fixed Production lock and
   193	protected-environment review still apply.
   194	
   195	The workflow must recheck the current version before mutation, plan the exact
   196	candidate, require provider/state agreement, apply through Alchemy and repeat
   197	provider and hosted proof. A source revert or successful workflow alone is not
   198	rollback proof.
   199	
   200	If the current provider version is unknown, Alchemy state differs from
   201	Cloudflare, or the workflow was interrupted during bootstrap, deploy, rollback
   202	or destroy, do not retry. Treat the outcome as unknown. Establish one
   203	authorised writer, read back Alchemy state and Cloudflare inventory, record the
   204	result, then choose a new exact recovery operation.
   205	
   206	## Escalation
   207	
   208	Escalate to the repository owner and deployment operation owner when candidate,
   209	stage, account, plan, state, provider, workflow or hosted identities disagree.
   210	Include the exact run and receipt IDs, the last known safe state, the stopped
   211	step, whether provider mutation may have started, and the proposed read-only
   212	checks. Do not include secrets or raw temporary URLs.
   213	
   214	Ask the protected-environment reviewer to reject the run if the requested
   215	operation is broader than the recorded authority. Ask the Cloudflare account
   216	owner to resolve an account or inventory mismatch. Ask the repository owner to
   217	approve any new workflow, credential scope, lock design or recovery mutation.
   218	
   219	## Stop conditions
   220	
   221	Stop before `versioning`, `commit`, `push`, `tag`, `release`,
   222	`registry-publication`, `deployment`, `provider-access` or
   223	`recovery-mutation` when its named authority is absent or unclear.
   224	
   225	Also stop when any of these occurs:
   226	
   227	- the candidate, workflow, pull request, stage, account or environment differs
   228	  from the approved identity;
   229	- Quality is missing, pending or failed;
   230	- the plan contains another resource, an unsupported action or malformed
   231	  beta.64 output;
   232	- replan differs from the accepted digest;
   233	- Alchemy state and Cloudflare readback disagree;
   234	- a matching manual mutation or workflow is already active;
   235	- a token, secret-bearing URL or machine-local path may have entered evidence;
   236	- bootstrap or provider mutation was interrupted and readback has not resolved
   237	  the outcome.
   238	
   239	## Limitations
   240	
   241	GitHub concurrency does not lock manual CLI mutation or another system. The
   242	repository does not use an external lease. Normal concurrent manual mutation
   243	is unsupported.
   244	
   245	Alchemy beta.64 bootstrap can change provider or state-store data before plan
   246	output. A plan-only workflow is therefore not wholly read-only. Remote and Bun
   247	caches can save time but do not replace frozen installation, live provider
   248	commands or receipt checks.
   249	
   250	The workers.dev readback covers the provider-managed host only. This runbook
   251	does not establish a custom domain. Retained artefacts may expire from GitHub;
   252	the repository fixture manifest keeps only sanitised plan bytes, source
   253	identity and digests, not credentials or full provider responses.
   254	
   255	## Non-claims
   256	
   257	Local checks do not prove a GitHub workflow ran. A GitHub success does not by

   262	This runbook does not authorise Production deploy, rollback, DNS change,
   263	credential creation or rotation, package publication, release, broad
   264	Cloudflare cleanup or unrelated provider mutation. Historical receipts do not
   265	prove current state, and the sanitised beta.64 fixtures prove parser
   266	compatibility only.

    64	## Core model
    65	
    66	```txt
    67	Schema-branded domain values
    68	  -> Schema.TaggedClass / Data.TaggedClass facts
    69	  -> Context.Tag fact and service providers
    70	  -> Layer.effect rule derivations
    71	  -> Layer-composed rule packs
    72	  -> typed calculator programs
    73	  -> trace, ledger, graph and report output
    74	```
    75	
    76	The planned engine is deterministic. Given the same accepted facts, rule
    77	layers, parameter layers, dates and policies, it must produce the same output
    78	and trace.

    81	
    82	Official calculations consume explicit input facts. Callers convert their application state into TaxKit-compatible input facts before invoking the engine.

    84	```txt

    86	  -> TaxKit rule layers
    87	  -> TaxKit calculators
    88	  -> reports, graph metadata and traces

    10	# Testing and quality
    11	
    12	TaxKit quality depends on deterministic calculation tests, package boundary
    13	tests, graph validation, trace snapshots, API/SDK parity and build/type health.
    14	
    15	## Scope
    16	
    17	This doc owns cross-cutting quality expectations. Detailed rule-package test
    18	requirements live in [Testing and validation](./testing-and-validation.md).
    19	
    20	## Main areas
    21	
    22	- rule-builder unit tests
    23	- ATO golden tests and known scenarios
    24	- property tests for thresholds and monotonicity
    25	- date-boundary tests
    26	- graph validation in CI
    27	- trace snapshots
    28	- package export and browser-safety tests
    29	- API and SDK parity tests

    31	## Current baseline
    32	
    33	The current repository baseline is canonical root verification:
    34	
    35	```bash
    36	bun run verification
    37	bun run knip:production
    38	bun run test:skills

    40	
    41	Root verification includes lint, format, both Knip graphs and workspace type
    42	checks. The development-aware graph covers repository tooling, tests and
    43	current application scaffolds. The production graph separately proves the
    44	eight code-bearing packages in the nine-artifact release closure,
    45	`@taxkit/scripts` exports and commands, and the standalone API runtime without
    46	test or development reachability. It also models the real `apps/docs`,
    47	`@taxkit/docs-content` and `@taxkit/docs-fumadocs` production entries,
    48	including the generated browser/server source consumed by the app and the
    49	build-time Vite/source config. `@taxkit/tsconfig` is JSON-only and remains

    52	graph by ownership. Root verification also typechecks and executes
    53	the root repository-path gate, which scans
    54	Git-tracked readable text and safely reports only repository-relative file,
    55	positive line and closed finding category. Binary files are identified by a
    56	NUL byte or failed strict UTF-8 decode and skipped. For skill governance it
    57	also runs `test:skills`, which validates required policy language and rejects
    58	stale provider-wrapper examples. The root graph also runs
    59	`check:harness-governance` exactly once. That Effect-native gate decodes the

    64	owners, self-contained references, portable runtime paths, and external
    65	non-claims. Its positive and adversarial corpus is owned by

    67	`check:harness-governance:types` and `test:harness-governance`.
    68	Target-specific requalification is separately owned by
    69	`check:harness-foundation-epoch` and its focused TypeScript check. That command

    73	not another root-verification or Quality-workflow edge.
    74	For docs, `apps/docs` type checking also

    10	# Docs deployment
    11	
    12	Owner: `taxkit-docs-deployment-operation-owner`
    13	
    14	## Identity and resource scope
    15	
    16	This runbook owns the TaxKit docs deployment made by root `alchemy.run.ts`.
    17	The current graph has one
    18	`Cloudflare.Website.Vite("DocsWebsite")` resource. Alchemy `2.0.0-beta.64`
    19	owns the Vite build, assets, Worker and resource lifecycle.
    20	
    21	Preview uses the exact `pr-N` stage for one same-repository pull request.
    22	Production uses the fixed `prod` stage. The runbook also covers the narrowly
    23	required Alchemy state store and read-only provider checks. It does not cover
    24	custom domains, DNS, unrelated Cloudflare resources, credentials, package
    25	publication or repository releases.
    26	
    27	## Preconditions
    28	
    29	Before an operation, read the current authority model at
    30	`docs/operations/authority-model.md`, the journey register at
    31	`docs/verification/docs-deployment-journeys.json`, and the history router at
    32	`docs/evidence/deployments/README.md`.
    33	
    34	Record these exact values before dispatch:
    35	
    36	- the named person approving the operation;
    37	- `plan`, `deploy`, `destroy` or `rollback`;
    38	- the exact candidate commit and reviewed default-branch workflow commit;
    39	- the pull-request number and `pr-N` stage, or the fixed `prod` stage;
    40	- the expected Cloudflare account and the protected GitHub environment;
    41	- the accepted plan digest and any earlier receipt identity required by the
    42	  workflow;
    43	- the expected postcondition, evidence route and recovery owner.
    44	
    45	The candidate must have a successful Quality result. Preview candidates must
    46	come from the same repository. Use the environment-scoped credential already
    47	attached to `taxkit-docs-preview` or `taxkit-docs-production`; do not copy it
    48	into a local file, command, log or receipt.
    49	
    50	## Authority
    51	
    52	Workflow access is not approval. The named approver must grant the exact
    53	operation, candidate, stage, provider account, protected environment and
    54	expected result. Production also needs the existing protected-environment
    55	review.
    56	
    57	Workflow YAML owns environment selection, GitHub permissions, concurrency,
    58	the provider commands and their order. The typed `workflow-evidence` command
    59	only calculates shared identities, decodes provider output and writes
    60	sanitised evidence. It cannot grant authority or run Alchemy, Wrangler or an
    61	arbitrary command.
    62	
    63	Alchemy login/bootstrap is mutation-capable in beta.64. It may refresh the
    64	provider credential, read a short-lived edge-preview secret, and create or
    65	upgrade state-store resources. Authorise it as part of the exact workflow
    66	operation. Its receipt proves only that the bounded step completed; it does
    67	not prove that no provider state changed.
    68	
    69	The Cloudflare token is available only to the named bootstrap, plan,
    70	replan/apply and destroy steps that need it. It must not be moved to a job,
    71	checkout, install, repository check, hosted proof or artefact upload.
    72	
    73	Production plan, deploy and rollback share the fixed non-cancellable
    74	`taxkit-docs-production-prod` group. Preview deploy and teardown share the
    75	exact non-cancellable `taxkit-docs-preview-pr-N` group. These GitHub locks do
    76	not cover a manual CLI. Do not run a manual Alchemy mutation while the matching
    77	workflow is queued or running. Break-glass manual work needs a separately
    78	authorised sole-writer period and state/provider readback before and after it.
    79	There is intentionally no external lease.
    80	
    81	## Procedure
    82	
    83	1. Confirm the preconditions and run the provider-free repository check
    84	   `bun run check:docs-deployment`. Run the required Quality checks for the
    85	   candidate. Local success does not prove GitHub, Alchemy or Cloudflare state.
    86	2. Dispatch `Docs Preview Deployment` or `Docs Production Deployment` from
    87	   reviewed default-branch workflow code. Supply every exact workflow input.
    88	   Use `operation=plan` first. Do not bypass the protected environment or edit
    89	   the workflow during a run.
    90	
    91	   Use these exact input names:
    92	
    93	   - Preview plan: `operation=plan`, `candidate_sha=<exact trusted PR head>` and
    94	     `pr_number=<positive same-repository PR number>`; leave
    95	     `accepted_plan_sha256` empty.
    96	   - Preview deploy: the same `candidate_sha` and `pr_number`,
    97	     `operation=deploy`, and
    98	     `accepted_plan_sha256=<digest from the accepted Preview plan run>`.
    99	   - Production plan: `operation=plan`,
   100	     `candidate_sha=<exact accepted candidate>`,
   101	     `accepted_preview_commit=<same exact candidate>`,
   102	     `accepted_preview_plan_sha256=<accepted Preview plan digest>`,
   103	     `accepted_preview_run_id=<successful Preview run>`, and
   104	     `accepted_preview_pr_number=<that Preview PR>`; leave
   105	     `accepted_plan_sha256`, `rollback_expected_current_version_id` and
   106	     `rollback_recovery_identity` empty.
   107	   - Production deploy: use the same five candidate/Preview values,
   108	     `operation=deploy`, and
   109	     `accepted_plan_sha256=<digest from the accepted Production plan run>`;
   110	     leave both rollback inputs empty.
   111	   - Production rollback: use the same five candidate/Preview values,
   112	     `operation=rollback`,
   113	     `accepted_plan_sha256=<digest from the accepted rollback plan run>`,
   114	     `rollback_expected_current_version_id=<fresh current Production version>`
   115	     and `rollback_recovery_identity=<identity from the accepted Preview
   116	     provider receipt>`.
   117	
   118	   Do not reuse a plan digest across a changed candidate, stage, lockfile or
   119	   configuration. A placeholder, shortened commit or caller-supplied value
   120	   without its named receipt is not an accepted input.
   121	3. The workflow checks candidate and Quality identity, installs frozen
   122	   dependencies, and runs provider-free docs checks. It then performs the
   123	   authorised bootstrap and runs `alchemy plan`. Alchemy owns the Vite build;
   124	   do not add a second build process.
   125	4. The typed evidence command decodes the raw plan with the single beta.64
   126	   parser. Accept only one `DocsWebsite` `create`, `update` or `noop` action for
   127	   deploy. The plan receipt must bind the exact candidate, lockfile,
   128	   configuration, stage and sanitised plan digest. Stop on another resource,
   129	   another action, malformed output or identity mismatch.
   130	5. Review the plan receipt. For deploy, dispatch the same workflow with the
   131	   exact accepted plan digest. The workflow replans and requires an equal
   132	   digest before apply. It then reads back the exact Alchemy stage, one
   133	   `DocsWebsite` Worker, Cloudflare deployment/version and workers.dev host,
   134	   and runs the hosted HTTP/browser proof.
   135	6. Keep the workflow receipt, provider readback and hosted proof separate.
   136	   Reconcile the completed GitHub run before accepting the receipt. A
   137	   successful source check is not provider proof; provider readback is not
   138	   public-host proof.
   139	7. When a same-repository Preview pull request closes, `Docs Preview Teardown`
   140	   runs from reviewed default-branch code in the same
   141	   `taxkit-docs-preview` environment. It rechecks the closed pull request,
   142	   takes the same `pr-N` lock, compares two destroy plans, destroys only that
   143	   stage, and proves state and Worker absence. An already absent stage is a
   144	   valid no-change result, not an invented delete.
   145	
   146	   The automatic close event supplies the PR and reviewed default-branch
   147	   identity. For a separately authorised manual teardown dispatch, supply
   148	   exactly `pr_number=<closed same-repository PR>` and
   149	   `reviewed_workflow_sha=<current reviewed main commit>`. Do not supply the PR
   150	   head as the workflow SHA.
   151	
   152	The shared Preview environment has no required reviewer, so automatic
   153	pull-request-close cleanup can use the same narrow credential as Preview
   154	deploy. A new receipt is not an open prerequisite for this same-environment
   155	automatic teardown. Require a fresh receipt if the environment, reviewer rule,
   156	credential scope, teardown source binding or lock control changes.
   157	
   158	For integrated local Cloudflare development, use the repository-owned
   159	`docs:dev:cloudflare` script. This is development only. It does not replace the
   160	workflow authority or receipt path.
   161	
   162	## Evidence and postcondition
   163	
   164	Retain sanitised receipts with the exact candidate, workflow run, operation,
   165	stage, account identity, plan digest, provider identity, postcondition and
   166	non-claims. Do not retain a bearer token, temporary secret-bearing URL, raw
   167	profile or machine-local path.
   168	
   169	The current journey definitions live at
   170	`docs/verification/docs-deployment-journeys.json`. Immutable dated provider,
   171	hosted, failure, cancellation, no-op, rollback and teardown records are routed
   172	through `docs/evidence/deployments/README.md`. Use those records as history;
   173	do not copy their old commands into this runbook.
   174	
   175	A deployment is accepted only when the exact workflow receipt, Alchemy stage,
   176	Cloudflare Worker/version and hosted result agree. Teardown is accepted only
   177	when the exact stage and Worker are absent, or when the decoded plan and
   178	readback both prove they were already absent. Preserve failed, cancelled,
   179	superseded and no-op attempts with their limits.
   180	
   181	### Retired history
   182	
   183	Some dated evidence refers to the former `DocsBuild` resource. That name is
   184	history only. It is not a current resource, command, plan expectation or
   185	recovery instruction.
   186	
   187	## Rollback
   188	
   189	For a normal Production rollback, use `Docs Production Deployment` with
   190	`operation=rollback`. Supply the exact accepted recovery candidate, its
   191	accepted Preview receipt identity, the expected current Production version and
   192	the recovery identity required by the workflow. The fixed Production lock and
   193	protected-environment review still apply.
   194	
   195	The workflow must recheck the current version before mutation, plan the exact
   196	candidate, require provider/state agreement, apply through Alchemy and repeat
   197	provider and hosted proof. A source revert or successful workflow alone is not
   198	rollback proof.
   199	
   200	If the current provider version is unknown, Alchemy state differs from
   201	Cloudflare, or the workflow was interrupted during bootstrap, deploy, rollback
   202	or destroy, do not retry. Treat the outcome as unknown. Establish one
   203	authorised writer, read back Alchemy state and Cloudflare inventory, record the
   204	result, then choose a new exact recovery operation.
   205	
   206	## Escalation
   207	
   208	Escalate to the repository owner and deployment operation owner when candidate,
   209	stage, account, plan, state, provider, workflow or hosted identities disagree.
   210	Include the exact run and receipt IDs, the last known safe state, the stopped
   211	step, whether provider mutation may have started, and the proposed read-only
   212	checks. Do not include secrets or raw temporary URLs.
   213	
   214	Ask the protected-environment reviewer to reject the run if the requested
   215	operation is broader than the recorded authority. Ask the Cloudflare account
   216	owner to resolve an account or inventory mismatch. Ask the repository owner to
   217	approve any new workflow, credential scope, lock design or recovery mutation.
   218	
   219	## Stop conditions
   220	
   221	Stop before `versioning`, `commit`, `push`, `tag`, `release`,
   222	`registry-publication`, `deployment`, `provider-access` or
   223	`recovery-mutation` when its named authority is absent or unclear.
   224	
   225	Also stop when any of these occurs:
   226	
   227	- the candidate, workflow, pull request, stage, account or environment differs
   228	  from the approved identity;
   229	- Quality is missing, pending or failed;
   230	- the plan contains another resource, an unsupported action or malformed
   231	  beta.64 output;
   232	- replan differs from the accepted digest;
   233	- Alchemy state and Cloudflare readback disagree;
   234	- a matching manual mutation or workflow is already active;
   235	- a token, secret-bearing URL or machine-local path may have entered evidence;
   236	- bootstrap or provider mutation was interrupted and readback has not resolved
   237	  the outcome.
   238	
   239	## Limitations
   240	
   241	GitHub concurrency does not lock manual CLI mutation or another system. The
   242	repository does not use an external lease. Normal concurrent manual mutation
   243	is unsupported.
   244	
   245	Alchemy beta.64 bootstrap can change provider or state-store data before plan
   246	output. A plan-only workflow is therefore not wholly read-only. Remote and Bun
   247	caches can save time but do not replace frozen installation, live provider
   248	commands or receipt checks.
   249	
   250	The workers.dev readback covers the provider-managed host only. This runbook
   251	does not establish a custom domain. Retained artefacts may expire from GitHub;
   252	the repository fixture manifest keeps only sanitised plan bytes, source
   253	identity and digests, not credentials or full provider responses.
   254	
   255	## Non-claims
   256	
   257	Local checks do not prove a GitHub workflow ran. A GitHub success does not by
   258	itself prove provider state. An Alchemy plan does not authorise apply. Provider
   259	readback does not prove the public site journey. A hosted HTTP response does not
   260	prove DNS or a custom domain.
   261	
   262	This runbook does not authorise Production deploy, rollback, DNS change,
   263	credential creation or rotation, package publication, release, broad
   264	Cloudflare cleanup or unrelated provider mutation. Historical receipts do not
   265	prove current state, and the sanitised beta.64 fixtures prove parser
   266	compatibility only.

     2	status: canonical
     3	last_reviewed: 2026-07-18
     4	source_of_truth: docs
     5	confidence: medium
     6	---
     7	
     8	# Configuration
     9	
    10	TaxKit configuration uses Effect `Config`, `ConfigProvider` and Schema.
    11	Package-owned runtime contracts define reusable schemas. Apps compose those
    12	schemas into runtime-specific configs and provide values from their own
    13	environment sources.
    14	
    15	## Ownership
    16	
    17	Packages that own a runtime contract MUST export the reusable config Schema,
    18	type and config fragments for that contract. If the package owns a public env
    19	namespace, such as `SERVICE_*`, the package config fragment MUST own that
    20	namespace too.
    21	
    22	Apps MUST define runtime-specific config modules that compose package schemas
    23	with app-local settings. Those modules own config sources such as process env
    24	or Vite env, app-local defaults and runtime-specific provider selection. They
    25	must not re-declare package-owned config keys or prefixes.
    26	
    27	## Pattern
    28	
    29	Package exports schema, type and a config fragment:
    30	
    31	```ts
    32	import { Config, Schema } from "effect";
    33	
    34	export const ServiceConfigSchema = Schema.Struct({
    35	  baseUrl: Schema.URLFromString,
    36	});
    37	
    38	export type ServiceConfig = Schema.Schema.Type<typeof ServiceConfigSchema>;
    39	
    40	export interface ServiceConfigFragment {
    41	  readonly service: ServiceConfig;
    42	}
    43	
    44	export const ServiceConfigFragment = {
    45	  service: Config.schema(ServiceConfigSchema),
    46	} satisfies Config.Wrap<ServiceConfigFragment>;
    47	
    48	export const ServiceServerEnvConfigFragment = {
    49	  service: Config.schema(ServiceConfigSchema).pipe(Config.nested("SERVICE")),
    50	} satisfies Config.Wrap<ServiceConfigFragment>;
    51	
    52	export const ServiceViteEnvConfigFragment = {
    53	  service: Config.schema(ServiceConfigSchema).pipe(
    54	    Config.nested("VITE_SERVICE")
    55	  ),
    56	} satisfies Config.Wrap<ServiceConfigFragment>;
    57	```
    58	
    59	App composes package config fragments into app config:
    60	
    61	```ts
    62	import { ServiceServerEnvConfigFragment } from "@owner/service/config";
    63	import { Config } from "effect";
    64	
    65	export const AppServerConfig = Config.all({
    66	  ...ServiceServerEnvConfigFragment,
    67	});
    68	```
    69	
    70	Runtime module provides values through a runtime source and generic naming
    71	convention:
    72	
    73	```ts
    74	import { ConfigProvider } from "effect";
    75	
    76	export const AppServerConfigProviderLive = ConfigProvider.layer(
    77	  ConfigProvider.fromEnv().pipe(ConfigProvider.constantCase)
    78	);
    79	```
    80	
    81	This maps a schema key such as `baseUrl` to `SERVICE_BASE_URL`.
    82	
    83	For Vite client env, use the same Effect env provider shape over
    84	`import.meta.env`:
    85	
    86	```ts
    87	export const AppClientConfigProviderLive = ConfigProvider.layer(
    88	  ConfigProvider.fromEnv({ env: import.meta.env }).pipe(
    89	    ConfigProvider.constantCase
    90	  )
    91	);
    92	```
    93	
    94	When composed with `ServiceViteEnvConfigFragment`, this maps `baseUrl` to
    95	`VITE_SERVICE_BASE_URL`.
    96	
    97	## Guardrails
    98	
    99	- MUST export schemas, types and keyed config fragments from package config
   100	  entrypoints.
   101	- Package config fragments MUST own package-specific config namespaces and env
   102	  prefixes such as `SERVICE` or `VITE_SERVICE`.
   103	- MUST compose package schemas from app-owned `config.server.ts` and
   104	  `config.client.ts` modules when runtime values differ. Apps should spread
   105	  package config fragments instead of re-declaring package-owned keys or
   106	  prefixes.
   107	- Apps SHOULD use `ConfigProvider.constantCase` at the runtime provider source
   108	  when env names follow a screaming-snake convention.
   109	- Avoid custom `ConfigProvider.mapInput` functions when package-owned
   110	  `Config.nested(...)` fragments and app-level `constantCase` express the
   111	  mapping.
   112	- Do not export package `Config` values that hard-code app-specific env names;
   113	  package-owned env namespaces are allowed and should live with the package
   114	  config fragment.
   115	- Keep one-off config error transformation inline at the runtime callsite.
   116	- Use Effect `Config`, `ConfigProvider`, `Schema`, `Layer` and platform
   117	  runtime primitives for configuration. Do not parse `process.env` or
   118	  `import.meta.env` by hand when an Effect config/schema composition can own
   119	  the shape.
   120	- Provider credentials and other semantic values use owner-named Schemas with
   121	  `Config.schema`; use `Schema.Redacted` or `Schema.RedactedFromValue` according
   122	  to the actual ingress representation. Do not expose primitive config values
   123	  through service APIs or unwrap secrets before final adapter construction.
   124	
   125	## Related Docs
   126	
   127	- [Effect services](./effect-services.md)
   128	- [Package ownership](./package-ownership.md)
   129	- [API and SDK](./api-and-sdk.md)
   130	- [Frontend](./frontend.md)

     9	
    10	# Deployment
    11	
    12	The docs app has a locally qualified Cloudflare Worker build and an Alchemy
    13	deployment composition. DCD-002 established one dated, exact-candidate Preview
    14	observation and safely removed that isolated stage. DCD-003 deployed the same
    15	accepted source to fixed stage `prod`, qualified a distinct successor through
    16	Preview and Production, and restored the accepted source through the normal
    17	Alchemy graph while preserving the Worker URL and state identity. Earlier
    18	failed Preview attempts remain historical disconfirming evidence, not current
    19	provider truth.
    20	
    21	## Scope
    22	
    23	This doc owns durable deployment and resource boundaries. Exact operator
    24	steps belong in the target-owned deployment runbook; current implementation
    25	intent and task state belong in the active SPEC and execution plan.
    26	
    27	## Current runtime shape
    28	
    29	- `apps/api` runs as a Bun HTTP server and serves `/api/*`.
    30	- `apps/web` builds through Vite/TanStack Start and calls `apps/api` over HTTP.
    31	- `apps/docs` owns one Cloudflare build mode. Exact
    32	  `@cloudflare/vite-plugin@1.47.0` emits `dist/server/index.js`, its server
    33	  modules and `dist/client` assets. The former docs-app Nitro/Vercel bridge was
    34	  retired after local parity; `apps/web` remains a separate Nitro owner.
    35	- Root `alchemy.run.ts` owns one `TaxKitDocsCloudflare` stack, branded
    36	  `pr-<number>` or `prod` stage admission, the mutation composition's
    37	  `Cloudflare.state()`, and one logical
    38	  `Cloudflare.Website.Vite("DocsWebsite")` resource. Alchemy injects its
    39	  Cloudflare Vite integration, builds the app, and owns the SSR Worker/assets
    40	  lifecycle and physical Worker name. The separate read-only inventory owner uses Alchemy's public
    41	  `makeHttpStateStore` after an Effect FileSystem/Schema boundary decodes the
    42	  account-matched cache, with a protected, redacted JSON fallback only when a
    43	  nested process cannot see that cache. Missing, malformed and unreadable
    44	  credential input remain distinct safe failures; neither path can bootstrap,
    45	  write or delete state.
    46	  The beta.64 Vite memo also includes the lockfile and the sibling
    47	  `docs-content` and `docs-fumadocs` package trees as native build inputs.
    48	- The Worker uses compatibility date `2026-06-24`, `nodejs_compat`, default
    49	  asset-first full-stack routing, a provider Worker URL, built-in invocation
    50	  logs and disabled traces. Hashed `/assets/*` responses are immutable.
    51	- The initial app has no runtime bindings, secrets or stateful application
    52	  service. KV, D1, R2, Durable Objects, Queues, Hyperdrive, Cron, custom
    53	  domains, DNS and third-party observability are absent.
    54	- `tools/docs-deployment/automation-register.json` and `controls.json` own the
    55	  Schema-decoded desired state for three workflow classes: Preview delivery,
    56	  Production delivery and exact-stage Preview teardown. All three are
    57	  `not-established` for the native one-resource graph until new matching
    58	  provider receipts are promoted. Historical two-resource and orphan receipts
    59	  remain evidence, not current automation state.
    60	- Five workflow receipt executables are narrow Bun adapters. Each decodes one
    61	  Config Schema from the host environment, reads receipt JSON and screenshot
    62	  bytes through the shared Effect FileSystem/Crypto boundary in
    63	  `workflow-check.boundary.ts`, preserves closed input/read/mismatch errors,
    64	  logs only safe operation and invariant identities through Effect Console,
    65	  and executes once through `BunRuntime.runMain`. Receipt decoding rejects
    66	  excess properties. The executables contain no direct environment, Bun file,
    67	  Promise, console or process-exit orchestration. This internal boundary does
    68	  not change workflow commands, the provider graph or historical receipts.
    69	- The four deployment and receipt workflows bind the approved Vercel Remote
    70	  Cache in read/write mode because they execute reviewed, exact-source workflow
    71	  code. Frozen Bun installation remains live and is preceded by a
    72	  content-addressed package-download cache. Preview, Production and teardown
    73	  also restore a content-addressed Playwright Chromium cache from the runner
    74	  temporary directory, then still run the pinned browser install. GitHub ref
    75	  scope isolates writes while allowing a matching default-branch cache to be
    76	  restored. The provider-free docs build uses the existing Turbo `docs#build`
    77	  task and its declared `dist/**` output.
    78	  Receipt-file checks, Alchemy plans and mutations, provider inventory, hosted
    79	  proof and receipt promotion enter through live or explicitly non-cacheable
    80	  tasks; no cache result can replace their current input or postcondition.
    81	- `@taxkit/api-http` builds as a package and exposes health, generated docs,
    82	  OpenAPI JSON, metadata and public calculation route contracts.
    83	- `@taxkit/sdk` builds as a private package for local and downstream
    84	  validation. It has not been published to npm.
    85	
    86	## Docs deployment graph
    87	
    88	```text
    89	frozen source and lock
    90	  -> root Cloudflare.Website.Vite("DocsWebsite")
    91	    -> Alchemy injects the Cloudflare Vite integration
    92	    -> Vite builds the TanStack SSR Worker and client assets
    93	    -> Alchemy applies one isolated pr-N or fixed prod website resource
    94	    -> provider/state readback identifies the workers.dev URL
    95	```
    96	
    97	The local command copies only emitted output to a temporary directory, removes
    98	checkout paths from the generated Wrangler config, strips provider credential
    99	variables, runs Wrangler dry-run and then runs the same no-bundle module graph
   100	under workerd. Local proof does not establish provider state or deployment.
   101	
   102	The repository-owned implementation and command map for deployment tooling is
   103	[`../../tools/docs-deployment/README.md`](../../tools/docs-deployment/README.md).
   104	
   105	`bun run check:docs-deployment-inventory` is the separate credentialed,
   106	provider-bound readback owner. It compares exact `TaxKitDocsCloudflare` state
   107	stages/resources with account Worker enumeration through public installed
   108	Alchemy APIs, fails on disagreement and emits only sanitized identities and
   109	non-claims. It is deliberately outside root verification and does not build,
   110	plan, apply, destroy or prove hosted behavior.
   111	
   112	Interactive use prints the encoded report. Workflows instead set
   113	`TAXKIT_DOCS_DEPLOYMENT_INVENTORY_REPORT` so the Effect runtime writes the
   114	machine-readable JSON directly to the named temporary file while Turbo keeps
   115	its own status text in the job log. Preview, Production and teardown must not
   116	parse Turbo's combined console output as provider evidence.

   118	Ephemeral GitHub runners do not retain Alchemy's derived
   119	`cloudflare-state-store` credential after a plan or apply. The three mutation
   120	workflows therefore run the supported `alchemy cloudflare bootstrap` operation
   121	with `CI=0` immediately before planning or teardown. A preceding supported
   122	`alchemy login` with `CI=1` writes only the `method: "env"` profile selector.
   123	Bootstrap is a mutation-capable control-plane operation: beta.64 may refresh
   124	credentials, use a short-lived edge-preview Worker to read the secret, and
   125	create or upgrade the state-store Worker before caching the account-matched
   126	credential on that runner. The inventory command reads the resulting cache
   127	under `CI=1`. This authority does not extend to the report-only workflow and no
   128	local OAuth profile is copied into CI.
   129	
   130	After bootstrap and plan complete, the closed `workflow-evidence` Effect
   131	command writes a sanitised bootstrap receipt. It binds the exact candidate,
   132	stage, workflow run, Alchemy `2.0.0-beta.64` and matching upstream source
   133	commit to those three allowed effects. It records state-store facts before and
   134	after as `not-observed`; successful bootstrap command completion is not a
   135	claim that no provider mutation occurred or that provider state was read back.
   136	
   137	The former scheduled GitHub/open-PR orphan classifier and nested subprocess
   138	boundary are retired. They did not provide a contributor-neutral lifecycle
   139	model. PR-close teardown remains the explicit Preview cleanup owner; retained
   140	orphan reports are immutable historical observations only.
   141	
   142	Preview deployment and exact-stage PR-close teardown share the
   143	`taxkit-docs-preview` GitHub environment and its narrow mutation credential.
   144	That environment has no required reviewer: the Preview dispatch or trusted
   145	same-repository PR-close event supplies operation authority, while reviewed
   146	source, exact `pr-N` decoding, the non-cancellable stage lock, equal plans and
   147	provider/state readback enforce the target. Production keeps its separate
   148	reviewer-protected environment. A GitHub environment controls credential
   149	custody; Alchemy stage identity controls which infrastructure can change.
   150	
   151	Preview and Production place `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` only on their named
   152	bootstrap, plan and replan/apply steps. Checkout, installation, provider-free
   153	builds, repository checks, hosted proof and artifact upload cannot read it.
   154	Production plan, deploy and rollback use the same fixed `prod` GitHub
   155	concurrency group with cancellation disabled. Preview and teardown keep their
   156	shared exact-`pr-N` non-cancellable group. These GitHub locks do not cover a
   157	manual Alchemy CLI process. Normal manual mutation must stop while the matching
   158	workflow is queued or running; break-glass recovery needs one separately
   159	authorised sole writer and state/provider readback before any retry.
   160	
   161	The accepted Preview requalification used candidate
   162	`d9cb8945529fb72158e59ca0daf02a98e1e4de1a` at deterministic stage `pr-1`.
   163	Alchemy created one prebuilt Worker/assets resource after two equal sanitized
   164	plans. Cloudflare readback and hosted proof agreed on the physical Worker,
   165	deployment/version, assets, provider URL, invocation-log persistence and
   166	disabled traces. The `/assets/*` cache contract required the root composition
   167	to pass the app-owned `_headers` file through the public Worker asset
   168	configuration. Exact-stage destroy subsequently removed the Preview Worker
   169	and stage resources. These dated observations prove neither current Preview
   170	availability nor Production.
   171	
   172	The earlier `0d714e6…` observation remains retained because it exposed the
   173	asset-header correction, but it lacked complete pre-mutation and
   174	candidate/screenshot/state bindings. It is trajectory evidence, not the
   175	accepted Preview chain.
   176	
   177	The accepted DCD-003 Production evidence first rebuilt exact Preview-qualified
   178	source `d9cb894…` into fixed stage `prod`. Cloudflare and Alchemy readback
   179	agreed on Worker
   180	`taxkitdocscloudflare-docswebsite-prod-ujphggiaxw5ryjev`, stable provider URL,
   181	assets, deployment/version and state instance. The full hosted and bounded
   182	screenshot contract passed.
   183	
   184	The normal rollback rehearsal then qualified repository successor `c99984c…`
   185	through a temporary isolated `pr-1` Preview, removed that Preview, deployed it

    10	# Controls and automation governance
    11	
    12	The Quality workflow is the executable CI owner for the local release-facing
    13	graph. It has read-only repository permission, a timeout, cancellation
    14	concurrency, an explicit `taxkit-ci-release-maintainer` pin-update owner, and
    15	full-SHA action pins. It invokes `bun run release:check -- --ci` on every
    16	configured pull request and on pushes to `main`; feature-branch pushes are
    17	intentionally covered by the pull-request event rather than running the same
    18	Quality graph a second time. There are deliberately no path filters, so a new
    19	or renamed release boundary cannot be skipped. The preceding bootstrap steps
    20	materialise complete `main` comparison history, resolve cache identities,
    21	perform a frozen Bun install and install Chromium plus its system packages
    22	through the app-local Playwright executable; a shallow checkout, cached
    23	`node_modules`, skipped install or floating browser-tool resolution fails
    24	policy. The Schema-decoded workflow,
    25	control register and negative corpus are owned by `tools/quality-workflow/` and
    26	run through `bun run check:quality-workflow`.
    27	
    28	Every eligible deterministic command under that graph is a Turbo task. Quality
    29	binds the Vercel team cache as read/write on all configured events.
    30	Same-repository pull requests and `main` receive the existing team-scoped
    31	remote-cache token; forks do not. The workflow policy rejects a missing
    32	binding, remote read-only regression, `pull_request_target` and step-level
    33	cache-mode overrides. This
    34	accepts that same-repository pull-request code can access the token. Local cache
    35	writes and the full uncached graph remain available if the credential or
    36	service is absent; cache success cannot replace a command exit status or
    37	release proof.
    38	
    39	Quality separately caches Bun package downloads and Playwright Chromium
    40	binaries through full-SHA GitHub cache restore/save actions. Bun's path comes
    41	from `bun pm cache`; Chromium uses an explicit `ms-playwright` directory under
    42	GitHub's runner temporary directory, outside the checkout. Keys include runner
    43	OS, architecture and `bun.lock`. The Bun key also includes `.bun-version`; the
    44	Chromium key includes the resolved app-local Playwright version. Event name is
    45	excluded so a pull request can restore a matching default-branch cache. GitHub
    46	ref scope keeps pull-request writes away from `main` and sibling pull requests.
    47	Cache operations are non-fatal, saves occur only after the matching install
    48	succeeds, and `bun install --frozen-lockfile` plus Playwright `--with-deps`
    49	always run. A restored Chromium binary does not prove system packages were
    50	installed.

     8	# TaxKit
     9	
    10	TaxKit is the public monorepo for the open-source tax engine, API, SDK and
    11	documentation site.
    12	
    13	The repo is early, but the main public integration surfaces now exist. The
    14	implemented surface is a standalone Bun API app, a TanStack Start web scaffold
    15	that calls that API, a Fumadocs-backed docs app, an Effect HTTP API package
    16	with health, generated docs, metadata and public calculation endpoints, a
    17	reusable calculator orchestration package, deterministic core engine
    18	primitives, Australian pay, income-tax and STSL rule packages, a private
    19	TypeScript SDK package, private `@taxkit/docs-content` and
    20	`@taxkit/docs-fumadocs` packages, shared testing helpers and shared TypeScript
    21	config, plus private Effect-native repository release orchestration in
    22	`@taxkit/scripts`. The SDK is implemented for local and downstream
    23	validation, but it is not published yet.
    24	
    25	## What exists today
    26	
    27	- [apps/api](./apps/api/README.md): standalone Bun process that owns API
    28	  startup, listening config and Effect runtime teardown for `/api/*`.
    29	- [apps/docs](./apps/docs/README.md): TanStack Start public documentation app
    30	  that renders MDX through package-owned docs content and reusable Fumadocs
    31	  helpers.
    32	- [apps/web](./apps/web/README.md): TanStack Start app that loads health data
    33	  from `apps/api` through server/client runtime boundaries.
    34	- [packages/api/http](./packages/api/http/README.md): Effect HTTP API contract,
    35	  generated docs, public calculator routes, thin handler adapters, server
    36	  handler exports and browser-safe client exports.
    37	- [packages/calculators](./packages/calculators/README.md): reusable public
    38	  calculator orchestration package for catalog metadata, graph construction,
    39	  calculation dispatch and schema-guided expected error shaping.
    40	- [packages/sdk/typescript](./packages/sdk/typescript/README.md): private
    41	  TypeScript SDK package with plain, safe-result, Effect and AU entrypoints.
    42	- [packages/docs-content](./packages/docs-content/README.md): private
    43	  source-only content package for docs frontmatter, navigation, validation,
    44	  generated source access and the docs content service.
    45	- [packages/docs-fumadocs](./packages/docs-fumadocs/README.md): private

    77	## Commands
    78	
    79	```sh
    80	bun install
    81	bun run --filter=api dev
    82	bun run --filter=web dev
    83	bun run --filter=docs dev
    84	bun run --filter=docs test:cloudflare-built
    85	bun run check:repository-paths
    86	bun run check:harness-governance
    87	bun run check:docs
    88	bun run knip:production
    89	bun run verification
    90	bun run test:skills
    91	bun run release:check
    92	bun run changeset
    93	bun run version-repo
    94	```
    95	
    96	`bun run --filter=api dev` serves the API through portless at
    97	`https://api.taxkit.localhost`. `bun run --filter=web dev` injects that
    98	portless URL into `TAXKIT_API_BASE_URL` and `VITE_TAXKIT_API_BASE_URL` before
    99	serving the web app at `https://taxkit.localhost`. `bun run --filter=docs dev`
   100	serves the public docs app at `https://docs.taxkit.localhost`. `bun run
   101	--filter=docs test:cloudflare-built` builds the exact Cloudflare target and
   102	exercises an isolated copy of its Worker/assets under local workerd; it does
   103	not access provider credentials or prove a deployment. `bun run
   104	check:repository-paths` rejects machine-local checkout references in tracked
   105	readable text without printing the matched private value. `bun run check:docs`
   106	checks maintainer metadata, links, documented commands, workspace README
   107	coverage, public/maintainer path separation, and generated-source ownership.
   108	It treats public content status as opaque and does not establish publication,
   109	availability, accuracy, or accepted-current truth. `bun run
   110	check:harness-governance` validates the repository-local harness profile,
   111	accepted HE crosswalk, skill-tree receipt, allowed overlays, relative Claude
   112	links, local skill references, critical journeys, and external non-claims. It
   113	does not read a global skill installation or establish remote Git, hosted CI,
   114	registry, release, deployment, provider, public-site, or external-consumer
   115	state. `bun run knip:production`
   116	checks the release-artifact package, repository command and
   117	API runtime graph without test or development reachability. `bun run
   118	verification` is the baseline verification command for documentation, package
   119	wiring and scaffold changes and includes repo-owned skill policy checks. `bun
   120	run test:skills` runs that focused stale-pattern suite directly. `bun run
   121	release:check` runs the complete ordered
   122	release evidence, including tests, builds, package artifacts, API smoke, docs
   123	browser proof and Changeset status.
   124	
   125	Deterministic repository commands run through Turbo, including the root
   126	validators used by `verification` and the app/package checks used by
   127	`release:check`. Token-bearing GitHub Quality runs may read and write Vercel
   128	Remote Cache on same-repository pull requests and `main`; fork pull requests
   129	receive no token and run the same full command graph locally. A missing token
   130	or cache service also falls back locally. Local remote-cache use is an explicit
   131	developer choice through `TURBO_TOKEN` and `TURBO_TEAM`. Never commit either
   132	credential or treat a cache hit as test, release, deployment or public
   133	availability proof.
   134	
   135	Quality also keeps separate GitHub caches for Bun package downloads and the
   136	Playwright Chromium binary. It does not cache `node_modules`: current warm
   137	hosted evidence shows the frozen Bun install takes only 1–2 seconds after the
   138	package cache restores, while the installed tree is about 1.4 GB. The workflow
   139	still runs frozen install plus Playwright system-dependency setup on every run.
   140	Keys use platform and dependency content, so pull requests may restore a
   141	matching cache saved by `main`. GitHub keeps pull-request writes on the
   142	pull-request merge ref, away from `main` and sibling pull requests. A miss or
   143	cache outage only changes download time.
   144	
   145	The trusted docs Preview, Production, teardown and receipt workflows use the
   146	same remote task cache for deterministic Turbo work. They use the same
   147	content-addressed Bun download keys, and browser workflows use the same
   148	content-addressed Chromium keys. GitHub ref scope controls writes. Exact
   149	candidate checks, provider plans or mutations, hosted readback and receipt
   150	promotion are always live and cannot be satisfied by a cache hit.
   151	
   152	Package-facing changes must include a Changeset. Use `bun run changeset` during
   153	implementation to record the user-facing package impact, and use
   154	`bun run version-repo` only when intentionally consuming pending Changesets into
   155	fixed release-train package versions and changelogs.

   142	`build` and its compatibility alias `build:cloudflare` select the exact
   143	official Cloudflare Vite adapter and emit the deployable no-bundle Worker at

   146	dry-run, and runs an isolated output-only copy under real workerd. It reuses the
   147	built-app behavioral contract for SSR, assets, server functions, 404,
   148	hydration, no-document navigation, accessibility and console cleanliness, and
   149	adds concurrent-isolate, filesystem, binding, compressed-upload-size, local

     8	# Configuration
     9	
    10	TaxKit configuration uses Effect `Config`, `ConfigProvider` and Schema.
    11	Package-owned runtime contracts define reusable schemas. Apps compose those
    12	schemas into runtime-specific configs and provide values from their own
    13	environment sources.
    14	
    15	## Ownership
    16	
    17	Packages that own a runtime contract MUST export the reusable config Schema,
    18	type and config fragments for that contract. If the package owns a public env
    19	namespace, such as `SERVICE_*`, the package config fragment MUST own that
    20	namespace too.
    21	
    22	Apps MUST define runtime-specific config modules that compose package schemas
    23	with app-local settings. Those modules own config sources such as process env
    24	or Vite env, app-local defaults and runtime-specific provider selection. They
    25	must not re-declare package-owned config keys or prefixes.
    26	
    27	## Pattern
    28	
    29	Package exports schema, type and a config fragment:
    30	
    31	```ts
    32	import { Config, Schema } from "effect";
    33	
    34	export const ServiceConfigSchema = Schema.Struct({
    35	  baseUrl: Schema.URLFromString,
    36	});
    37	
    38	export type ServiceConfig = Schema.Schema.Type<typeof ServiceConfigSchema>;
    39	
    40	export interface ServiceConfigFragment {
    41	  readonly service: ServiceConfig;
    42	}
    43	
    44	export const ServiceConfigFragment = {
    45	  service: Config.schema(ServiceConfigSchema),
    46	} satisfies Config.Wrap<ServiceConfigFragment>;
    47	
    48	export const ServiceServerEnvConfigFragment = {
    49	  service: Config.schema(ServiceConfigSchema).pipe(Config.nested("SERVICE")),
    50	} satisfies Config.Wrap<ServiceConfigFragment>;
    51	
    52	export const ServiceViteEnvConfigFragment = {
    53	  service: Config.schema(ServiceConfigSchema).pipe(
    54	    Config.nested("VITE_SERVICE")
    55	  ),
    56	} satisfies Config.Wrap<ServiceConfigFragment>;
    57	```
    58	
    59	App composes package config fragments into app config:
    60	
    61	```ts
    62	import { ServiceServerEnvConfigFragment } from "@owner/service/config";
    63	import { Config } from "effect";
    64	
    65	export const AppServerConfig = Config.all({
    66	  ...ServiceServerEnvConfigFragment,
    67	});
    68	```
    69	
    70	Runtime module provides values through a runtime source and generic naming
    71	convention:
    72	
    73	```ts
    74	import { ConfigProvider } from "effect";
    75	
    76	export const AppServerConfigProviderLive = ConfigProvider.layer(
    77	  ConfigProvider.fromEnv().pipe(ConfigProvider.constantCase)
    78	);
    79	```
    80	
    81	This maps a schema key such as `baseUrl` to `SERVICE_BASE_URL`.
    82	
    83	For Vite client env, use the same Effect env provider shape over
    84	`import.meta.env`:
    85	
    86	```ts
    87	export const AppClientConfigProviderLive = ConfigProvider.layer(
    88	  ConfigProvider.fromEnv({ env: import.meta.env }).pipe(
    89	    ConfigProvider.constantCase
    90	  )
    91	);
    92	```
    93	
    94	When composed with `ServiceViteEnvConfigFragment`, this maps `baseUrl` to
    95	`VITE_SERVICE_BASE_URL`.
    96	
    97	## Guardrails
    98	
    99	- MUST export schemas, types and keyed config fragments from package config
   100	  entrypoints.
   101	- Package config fragments MUST own package-specific config namespaces and env
   102	  prefixes such as `SERVICE` or `VITE_SERVICE`.
   103	- MUST compose package schemas from app-owned `config.server.ts` and
   104	  `config.client.ts` modules when runtime values differ. Apps should spread
   105	  package config fragments instead of re-declaring package-owned keys or
   106	  prefixes.
   107	- Apps SHOULD use `ConfigProvider.constantCase` at the runtime provider source
   108	  when env names follow a screaming-snake convention.
   109	- Avoid custom `ConfigProvider.mapInput` functions when package-owned
   110	  `Config.nested(...)` fragments and app-level `constantCase` express the
   111	  mapping.
   112	- Do not export package `Config` values that hard-code app-specific env names;
   113	  package-owned env namespaces are allowed and should live with the package
   114	  config fragment.
   115	- Keep one-off config error transformation inline at the runtime callsite.
   116	- Use Effect `Config`, `ConfigProvider`, `Schema`, `Layer` and platform
   117	  runtime primitives for configuration. Do not parse `process.env` or
   118	  `import.meta.env` by hand when an Effect config/schema composition can own
   119	  the shape.
   120	- Provider credentials and other semantic values use owner-named Schemas with
   121	  `Config.schema`; use `Schema.Redacted` or `Schema.RedactedFromValue` according
   122	  to the actual ingress representation. Do not expose primitive config values
   123	  through service APIs or unwrap secrets before final adapter construction.
   124

   128	- [Package ownership](./package-ownership.md)
   129	- [API and SDK](./api-and-sdk.md)
   130	- [Frontend](./frontend.md)

    10	# Controls and automation governance
    11	
    12	The Quality workflow is the executable CI owner for the local release-facing
    13	graph. It has read-only repository permission, a timeout, cancellation
    14	concurrency, an explicit `taxkit-ci-release-maintainer` pin-update owner, and
    15	full-SHA action pins. It invokes `bun run release:check -- --ci` on every
    16	configured pull request and on pushes to `main`; feature-branch pushes are
    17	intentionally covered by the pull-request event rather than running the same
    18	Quality graph a second time. There are deliberately no path filters, so a new
    19	or renamed release boundary cannot be skipped. The preceding bootstrap steps
    20	materialise complete `main` comparison history, resolve cache identities,
    21	perform a frozen Bun install and install Chromium plus its system packages
    22	through the app-local Playwright executable; a shallow checkout, cached
    23	`node_modules`, skipped install or floating browser-tool resolution fails
    24	policy. The Schema-decoded workflow,
    25	control register and negative corpus are owned by `tools/quality-workflow/` and
    26	run through `bun run check:quality-workflow`.
    27	
    28	Every eligible deterministic command under that graph is a Turbo task. Quality
    29	binds the Vercel team cache as read/write on all configured events.
    30	Same-repository pull requests and `main` receive the existing team-scoped
    31	remote-cache token; forks do not. The workflow policy rejects a missing
    32	binding, remote read-only regression, `pull_request_target` and step-level
    33	cache-mode overrides. This
    34	accepts that same-repository pull-request code can access the token. Local cache
    35	writes and the full uncached graph remain available if the credential or
    36	service is absent; cache success cannot replace a command exit status or
    37	release proof.
    38	
    39	Quality separately caches Bun package downloads and Playwright Chromium
    40	binaries through full-SHA GitHub cache restore/save actions. Bun's path comes
    41	from `bun pm cache`; Chromium uses an explicit `ms-playwright` directory under
    42	GitHub's runner temporary directory, outside the checkout. Keys include runner
    43	OS, architecture and `bun.lock`. The Bun key also includes `.bun-version`; the
    44	Chromium key includes the resolved app-local Playwright version. Event name is
    45	excluded so a pull request can restore a matching default-branch cache. GitHub
    46	ref scope keeps pull-request writes away from `main` and sibling pull requests.
    47	Cache operations are non-fatal, saves occur only after the matching install
    48	succeeds, and `bun install --frozen-lockfile` plus Playwright `--with-deps`
    49	always run. A restored Chromium binary does not prove system packages were
    50	installed.

    56	| Turbo task, cache credential or event mode changes; a fork or `pull_request_target` receives the credential, missing cache blocks execution, or a hit is treated as proof | `controls.json` entry `turbo-remote-cache-boundary`; `policy.test.ts`, `check:quality-workflow`, full local fallback and exact mode recovery | Turbo config, task input/output, workflow event, contributor trust, credential or fallback change | A stronger token-bearing cache authority and fallback control replaces this contract. |
    57	| Bun or Chromium cache changes; `node_modules`, an incompatible binary, skipped install or fatal cache outage enters Quality | `controls.json` entry `quality-dependency-cache-boundary`; `policy.test.ts`, `check:quality-workflow`, exact path/key/order and cache-removal recovery | Bun/Playwright version, lockfile, runner platform, cache action, key, path, event or install change | A stronger content-addressed dependency-cache control replaces this contract. |

     8	# TaxKit
     9	
    10	TaxKit is the public monorepo for the open-source tax engine, API, SDK and
    11	documentation site.
    12	
    13	The repo is early, but the main public integration surfaces now exist. The
    14	implemented surface is a standalone Bun API app, a TanStack Start web scaffold
    15	that calls that API, a Fumadocs-backed docs app, an Effect HTTP API package
    16	with health, generated docs, metadata and public calculation endpoints, a
    17	reusable calculator orchestration package, deterministic core engine
    18	primitives, Australian pay, income-tax and STSL rule packages, a private
    19	TypeScript SDK package, private `@taxkit/docs-content` and
    20	`@taxkit/docs-fumadocs` packages, shared testing helpers and shared TypeScript
    21	config, plus private Effect-native repository release orchestration in
    22	`@taxkit/scripts`. The SDK is implemented for local and downstream
    23	validation, but it is not published yet.
    24	
    25	## What exists today
    26	
    27	- [apps/api](./apps/api/README.md): standalone Bun process that owns API
    28	  startup, listening config and Effect runtime teardown for `/api/*`.
    29	- [apps/docs](./apps/docs/README.md): TanStack Start public documentation app
    30	  that renders MDX through package-owned docs content and reusable Fumadocs
    31	  helpers.
    32	- [apps/web](./apps/web/README.md): TanStack Start app that loads health data
    33	  from `apps/api` through server/client runtime boundaries.
    34	- [packages/api/http](./packages/api/http/README.md): Effect HTTP API contract,
    35	  generated docs, public calculator routes, thin handler adapters, server
    36	  handler exports and browser-safe client exports.
    37	- [packages/calculators](./packages/calculators/README.md): reusable public
    38	  calculator orchestration package for catalog metadata, graph construction,
    39	  calculation dispatch and schema-guided expected error shaping.
    40	- [packages/sdk/typescript](./packages/sdk/typescript/README.md): private
    41	  TypeScript SDK package with plain, safe-result, Effect and AU entrypoints.
    42	- [packages/docs-content](./packages/docs-content/README.md): private
    43	  source-only content package for docs frontmatter, navigation, validation,
    44	  generated source access and the docs content service.
    45	- [packages/docs-fumadocs](./packages/docs-fumadocs/README.md): private
    46	  reusable package for generic Fumadocs configuration, source adapters and
    47	  MDX render primitives.
    48	- [packages/core](./packages/core/README.md): deterministic engine primitives,
    49	  schema-backed facts, rule descriptors, graph validation, trace and ledger
    50	  contracts and calculation engine service.
    51	- `packages/rules/au/*`: implemented Australian pay, annual income-tax and
    52	  STSL rule packages with Effect rule layers, official parameter services,
    53	  calculators and golden tests.
    54	- [packages/testing](./packages/testing/README.md): shared test helpers for
    55	  workspace packages.
    56	- [packages/tsconfig](./packages/tsconfig/README.md): shared TypeScript config
    57	  presets.
    58	- [packages/scripts](./packages/scripts/README.md): private Effect-native
    59	  orchestration package for the complete local release-readiness command.
    60	- [packages/ui](./packages/ui/README.md): documented planned shared UI
    61	  ownership without a package manifest or runtime code yet.

    77	## Commands
    78	
    79	```sh
    80	bun install
    81	bun run --filter=api dev
    82	bun run --filter=web dev
    83	bun run --filter=docs dev
    84	bun run --filter=docs test:cloudflare-built
    85	bun run check:repository-paths
    86	bun run check:harness-governance
    87	bun run check:docs
    88	bun run knip:production
    89	bun run verification
    90	bun run test:skills
    91	bun run release:check
    92	bun run changeset
    93	bun run version-repo
    94	```
    95	
    96	`bun run --filter=api dev` serves the API through portless at
    97	`https://api.taxkit.localhost`. `bun run --filter=web dev` injects that
    98	portless URL into `TAXKIT_API_BASE_URL` and `VITE_TAXKIT_API_BASE_URL` before
    99	serving the web app at `https://taxkit.localhost`. `bun run --filter=docs dev`
   100	serves the public docs app at `https://docs.taxkit.localhost`. `bun run
   101	--filter=docs test:cloudflare-built` builds the exact Cloudflare target and
   102	exercises an isolated copy of its Worker/assets under local workerd; it does
   103	not access provider credentials or prove a deployment. `bun run
   104	check:repository-paths` rejects machine-local checkout references in tracked
   105	readable text without printing the matched private value. `bun run check:docs`
   106	checks maintainer metadata, links, documented commands, workspace README
   107	coverage, public/maintainer path separation, and generated-source ownership.
   108	It treats public content status as opaque and does not establish publication,
   109	availability, accuracy, or accepted-current truth. `bun run
   110	check:harness-governance` validates the repository-local harness profile,
   111	accepted HE crosswalk, skill-tree receipt, allowed overlays, relative Claude
   112	links, local skill references, critical journeys, and external non-claims. It
   113	does not read a global skill installation or establish remote Git, hosted CI,
   114	registry, release, deployment, provider, public-site, or external-consumer
   115	state. `bun run knip:production`
   116	checks the release-artifact package, repository command and
   117	API runtime graph without test or development reachability. `bun run
   118	verification` is the baseline verification command for documentation, package
   119	wiring and scaffold changes and includes repo-owned skill policy checks. `bun
   120	run test:skills` runs that focused stale-pattern suite directly. `bun run
   121	release:check` runs the complete ordered
   122	release evidence, including tests, builds, package artifacts, API smoke, docs
   123	browser proof and Changeset status.
   124	
   125	Deterministic repository commands run through Turbo, including the root
   126	validators used by `verification` and the app/package checks used by
   127	`release:check`. Token-bearing GitHub Quality runs may read and write Vercel
   128	Remote Cache on same-repository pull requests and `main`; fork pull requests
   129	receive no token and run the same full command graph locally. A missing token
   130	or cache service also falls back locally. Local remote-cache use is an explicit
   131	developer choice through `TURBO_TOKEN` and `TURBO_TEAM`. Never commit either
   132	credential or treat a cache hit as test, release, deployment or public
   133	availability proof.
   134	
   135	Quality also keeps separate GitHub caches for Bun package downloads and the
   136	Playwright Chromium binary. It does not cache `node_modules`: current warm
   137	hosted evidence shows the frozen Bun install takes only 1–2 seconds after the
   138	package cache restores, while the installed tree is about 1.4 GB. The workflow
   139	still runs frozen install plus Playwright system-dependency setup on every run.
   140	Keys use platform and dependency content, so pull requests may restore a

     8	# Configuration
     9	
    10	TaxKit configuration uses Effect `Config`, `ConfigProvider` and Schema.
    11	Package-owned runtime contracts define reusable schemas. Apps compose those
    12	schemas into runtime-specific configs and provide values from their own
    13	environment sources.
    14	
    15	## Ownership
    16	
    17	Packages that own a runtime contract MUST export the reusable config Schema,
    18	type and config fragments for that contract. If the package owns a public env
    19	namespace, such as `SERVICE_*`, the package config fragment MUST own that
    20	namespace too.
    21	
    22	Apps MUST define runtime-specific config modules that compose package schemas
    23	with app-local settings. Those modules own config sources such as process env
    24	or Vite env, app-local defaults and runtime-specific provider selection. They
    25	must not re-declare package-owned config keys or prefixes.
    26	
    27	## Pattern
    28	
    29	Package exports schema, type and a config fragment:
    30	
    31	```ts
    32	import { Config, Schema } from "effect";
    33	
    34	export const ServiceConfigSchema = Schema.Struct({
    35	  baseUrl: Schema.URLFromString,
    36	});
    37	
    38	export type ServiceConfig = Schema.Schema.Type<typeof ServiceConfigSchema>;
    39	
    40	export interface ServiceConfigFragment {
    41	  readonly service: ServiceConfig;
    42	}
    43	
    44	export const ServiceConfigFragment = {
    45	  service: Config.schema(ServiceConfigSchema),
    46	} satisfies Config.Wrap<ServiceConfigFragment>;
    47	
    48	export const ServiceServerEnvConfigFragment = {
    49	  service: Config.schema(ServiceConfigSchema).pipe(Config.nested("SERVICE")),
    50	} satisfies Config.Wrap<ServiceConfigFragment>;
    51	
    52	export const ServiceViteEnvConfigFragment = {
    53	  service: Config.schema(ServiceConfigSchema).pipe(
    54	    Config.nested("VITE_SERVICE")
    55	  ),
    56	} satisfies Config.Wrap<ServiceConfigFragment>;
    57	```
    58	
    59	App composes package config fragments into app config:
    60	
    61	```ts
    62	import { ServiceServerEnvConfigFragment } from "@owner/service/config";
    63	import { Config } from "effect";
    64	
    65	export const AppServerConfig = Config.all({
    66	  ...ServiceServerEnvConfigFragment,
    67	});
    68	```
    69	
    70	Runtime module provides values through a runtime source and generic naming
    71	convention:
    72	
    73	```ts
    74	import { ConfigProvider } from "effect";
    75	
    76	export const AppServerConfigProviderLive = ConfigProvider.layer(
    77	  ConfigProvider.fromEnv().pipe(ConfigProvider.constantCase)
    78	);
    79	```
    80	
    81	This maps a schema key such as `baseUrl` to `SERVICE_BASE_URL`.
    82	
    83	For Vite client env, use the same Effect env provider shape over
    84	`import.meta.env`:
    85	
    86	```ts
    87	export const AppClientConfigProviderLive = ConfigProvider.layer(
    88	  ConfigProvider.fromEnv({ env: import.meta.env }).pipe(
    89	    ConfigProvider.constantCase
    90	  )
    91	);
    92	```
    93	
    94	When composed with `ServiceViteEnvConfigFragment`, this maps `baseUrl` to
    95	`VITE_SERVICE_BASE_URL`.
    96	
    97	## Guardrails
    98	
    99	- MUST export schemas, types and keyed config fragments from package config
   100	  entrypoints.
   101	- Package config fragments MUST own package-specific config namespaces and env
   102	  prefixes such as `SERVICE` or `VITE_SERVICE`.
   103	- MUST compose package schemas from app-owned `config.server.ts` and
   104	  `config.client.ts` modules when runtime values differ. Apps should spread
   105	  package config fragments instead of re-declaring package-owned keys or
   106	  prefixes.
   107	- Apps SHOULD use `ConfigProvider.constantCase` at the runtime provider source
   108	  when env names follow a screaming-snake convention.
   109	- Avoid custom `ConfigProvider.mapInput` functions when package-owned
   110	  `Config.nested(...)` fragments and app-level `constantCase` express the
   111	  mapping.
   112	- Do not export package `Config` values that hard-code app-specific env names;
   113	  package-owned env namespaces are allowed and should live with the package
   114	  config fragment.
   115	- Keep one-off config error transformation inline at the runtime callsite.
   116	- Use Effect `Config`, `ConfigProvider`, `Schema`, `Layer` and platform
   117	  runtime primitives for configuration. Do not parse `process.env` or
   118	  `import.meta.env` by hand when an Effect config/schema composition can own
   119	  the shape.
   120	- Provider credentials and other semantic values use owner-named Schemas with
   121	  `Config.schema`; use `Schema.Redacted` or `Schema.RedactedFromValue` according
   122	  to the actual ingress representation. Do not expose primitive config values
   123	  through service APIs or unwrap secrets before final adapter construction.

     8	# Configuration
     9	
    10	TaxKit configuration uses Effect `Config`, `ConfigProvider` and Schema.
    11	Package-owned runtime contracts define reusable schemas. Apps compose those
    12	schemas into runtime-specific configs and provide values from their own
    13	environment sources.
    14	
    15	## Ownership
    16	
    17	Packages that own a runtime contract MUST export the reusable config Schema,
    18	type and config fragments for that contract. If the package owns a public env
    19	namespace, such as `SERVICE_*`, the package config fragment MUST own that
    20	namespace too.
    21	
    22	Apps MUST define runtime-specific config modules that compose package schemas
    23	with app-local settings. Those modules own config sources such as process env
    24	or Vite env, app-local defaults and runtime-specific provider selection. They
    25	must not re-declare package-owned config keys or prefixes.
    26	
    27	## Pattern
    28	
    29	Package exports schema, type and a config fragment:
    30	
    31	```ts
    32	import { Config, Schema } from "effect";
    33	
    34	export const ServiceConfigSchema = Schema.Struct({
    35	  baseUrl: Schema.URLFromString,
    36	});
    37	
    38	export type ServiceConfig = Schema.Schema.Type<typeof ServiceConfigSchema>;
    39	
    40	export interface ServiceConfigFragment {
    41	  readonly service: ServiceConfig;
    42	}
    43	
    44	export const ServiceConfigFragment = {
    45	  service: Config.schema(ServiceConfigSchema),
    46	} satisfies Config.Wrap<ServiceConfigFragment>;
    47	
    48	export const ServiceServerEnvConfigFragment = {
    49	  service: Config.schema(ServiceConfigSchema).pipe(Config.nested("SERVICE")),
    50	} satisfies Config.Wrap<ServiceConfigFragment>;
    51	
    52	export const ServiceViteEnvConfigFragment = {
    53	  service: Config.schema(ServiceConfigSchema).pipe(
    54	    Config.nested("VITE_SERVICE")
    55	  ),
    56	} satisfies Config.Wrap<ServiceConfigFragment>;
    57	```
    58	
    59	App composes package config fragments into app config:
    60	
    61	```ts
    62	import { ServiceServerEnvConfigFragment } from "@owner/service/config";
    63	import { Config } from "effect";
    64	
    65	export const AppServerConfig = Config.all({
    66	  ...ServiceServerEnvConfigFragment,
    67	});
    68	```
    69	
    70	Runtime module provides values through a runtime source and generic naming
    71	convention:
    72	
    73	```ts
    74	import { ConfigProvider } from "effect";
    75	
    76	export const AppServerConfigProviderLive = ConfigProvider.layer(
    77	  ConfigProvider.fromEnv().pipe(ConfigProvider.constantCase)
    78	);
    79	```
    80	
    81	This maps a schema key such as `baseUrl` to `SERVICE_BASE_URL`.
    82	
    83	For Vite client env, use the same Effect env provider shape over
    84	`import.meta.env`:

    86	```ts

    88	  ConfigProvider.fromEnv({ env: import.meta.env }).pipe(
    89	    ConfigProvider.constantCase
    90	  )
    91	);
    92	```
    93	
    94	When composed with `ServiceViteEnvConfigFragment`, this maps `baseUrl` to
    95	`VITE_SERVICE_BASE_URL`.

    97	## Guardrails
    98	
    99	- MUST export schemas, types and keyed config fragments from package config
   100	  entrypoints.
   101	- Package config fragments MUST own package-specific config namespaces and env
   102	  prefixes such as `SERVICE` or `VITE_SERVICE`.

   104	  `config.client.ts` modules when runtime values differ. Apps should spread
   105	  package config fragments instead of re-declaring package-owned keys or
   106	  prefixes.

   108	  when env names follow a screaming-snake convention.
