    67	              -> TaxKit generated collection adapter
    68	              -> packages/docs-content/.source/server
    69	              -> schema-decoded navigation.json representation
    70	        -> schema-encoded Exit representation
    71	    -> TanStack SSR hydration or client-navigation transport
    72	      -> direct route-root restore and Result match
    73	        -> @taxkit/docs-content/client
    74	          -> Fumadocs compiled MDX module
    75	        -> @taxkit/docs-fumadocs/render
    76	        -> app-local MDX component map
    77	```
    78	
    79	## Commands
    80	
    81	```txt
    82	bun run --filter=docs dev
    83	bun run --filter=docs dev:vite
    84	bun run --filter=docs check-import-boundaries
    85	bun run --filter=docs test
    86	bun run --filter=docs test:browser
    87	bun run --filter=docs test:built
    88	bun run --filter=docs test:cloudflare-built
    89	bun run --filter=docs test:cloudflare-hosted
    90	bun run --filter=docs build:cloudflare
    91	bun run --filter=docs check-types
    92	bun run --filter=docs build
    93	bun run --filter=docs preview
    94	bun run --filter=@taxkit/docs-content check-examples
    95	bun run docs:validate
    96	```
    97	
    98	`dev` is the authoritative Alchemy-managed Cloudflare development path and
    99	runs `alchemy dev` from the repository root. `dev:vite` is the fast,
   100	infrastructure-free portless Vite path at `https://docs.taxkit.localhost`.
   101	Alchemy beta.64 injects its Cloudflare Vite plugin for the native resource;
   102	standalone Vite installs the same official plugin only when the documented
   103	`ALCHEMY_CLOUDFLARE_VITE_INJECTED` guard is absent.
   104	
   105	`@taxkit/docs-content` `check-types` includes `check-examples`, so the
   106	package-owned public examples stay connected to current SDK/API/calculator
   107	exports.
   108	
   109	Run `build` before `preview`. Turbo orders the package-owned content build
   110	before the app, while a direct Vite app build regenerates the same package-owned
   111	source through `source.config.ts`. The config-only Fumadocs export is
   112	source-owned, so a clean direct app build does not require a prebuilt workspace
   113	artifact. The Vite config resolves the Fumadocs config and generated-source
   114	paths from its own file location, so the standalone and repository-root
   115	Alchemy builds use the same generated source even after a cached package
   116	build. `dev:vite` and `preview` expose the app through portless.
   117	
   118	`test:browser` runs the programmatic TanStack client-route harness in Chromium.
   119	It proves success, expected failures, malformed transport and framework error
   120	boundaries after `Route.useLoaderData`; it does not prove SSR or hydration. Use
   121	the built app for initial SSR, hydration and real client-navigation proof.
   122	
   123	`test:built` builds the production Cloudflare Worker/assets output and executes
   124	the generated no-bundle Worker through a command-owned local workerd server. It
   125	asserts a known page in the HTTP response before browser JavaScript, hydration
   126	without warnings or errors, real sidebar and authored-MDX client transitions
   127	with zero document requests, browser back/forward, heading focus without
   128	stealing initial-hydration focus, pending state, framework-native client
   129	not-found behavior and a direct HTTP 404. It also checks the skip link,
   130	landmarks, labelled/current navigation, mobile disclosure, representative
   131	contrast, reduced-motion rendering, immutable asset headers, runtime reuse,
   132	filesystem isolation and compressed upload size. The command owns
   133	browser/workerd cleanup. `test:cloudflare-built` remains an explicit alias for
   134	the same canonical proof command. Add `-- --screenshots` for the bounded
   135	candidate-bound desktop/mobile PNG and digest manifest under ignored
   136	`tmp/docs-cloudflare/`. The desktop capture shows the representative guide;
   137	the mobile capture shows its open navigation state. Screenshot review
   138	supplements these behavioral assertions and cannot prove request type, focus
   139	behavior, contrast, motion suppression, HTTP status, hydration, console
   140	cleanliness or hosted behavior.
   141	
   142	`build` and its compatibility alias `build:cloudflare` select the exact
   143	official Cloudflare Vite adapter and emit the deployable no-bundle Worker at
   144	`dist/server/index.js` plus `dist/client` assets. The canonical built proof
   145	strips provider credentials from the child environment, performs a Wrangler
   146	dry-run, and runs an isolated output-only copy under real workerd. It reuses the
   147	built-app behavioral contract for SSR, assets, server functions, 404,
   148	hydration, no-document navigation, accessibility and console cleanliness, and
   149	adds concurrent-isolate, filesystem, binding, compressed-upload-size, local
   150	readiness-timing and immutable asset-header oracles. The local timing is not a
   151	Cloudflare CPU-startup-limit receipt. The exact verified invocation is:
   152	
   153	```sh
   154	bun run --filter=docs test:cloudflare-built
   155	```
   156	
   157	This is local workerd evidence only. It does not prove Alchemy state, a
   158	Cloudflare deployment, a `workers.dev` URL, Preview, Production or rollback.
   159	The former docs-app Nitro/Vercel bridge has been removed after local parity;
   160	Nitro remains an independent owner only where another application still uses
   161	it. Final hosted requalification of the exact retirement candidate and the
   162	report-only Alchemy state boundary remain separate claims.
   163	
   164	Root `alchemy.run.ts` uses public Alchemy
   165	`Cloudflare.Website.Vite("DocsWebsite")`. Alchemy owns Vite build execution,
   166	assets, the SSR Worker lifecycle and the physical Worker name as one logical
   167	resource. Its beta.64 memo includes the lockfile and both sibling docs
   168	packages, so those authored inputs participate in Alchemy's resource input.
   169	The standalone `build:cloudflare` alias and workerd harness are provider-free
   170	preflight proof; their `dist/**` output is not asserted to be the exact artifact
   171	produced inside an Alchemy plan/apply. `.wrangler/**` and `dist/**` remain
   172	ignored generated output and are never deployment receipts.
   173	
   174	Exact Preview, Production, teardown, rollback and Alchemy-state operations
   175	belong to `docs/runbooks/docs-deployment.md`; dated sanitized observations
   176	belong below `docs/evidence/deployments/`. The hosted harness requires the
   177	read-back URL, candidate, stage, environment, plan/config/lock/deployment-input
   178	digests, Worker/deployment/version identities, evidence directory and rollback
   179	identity. Effect Config and the owning Schemas decode those values plus the
   180	whole-number retry count and delay before Chromium starts. Preview must pair
   181	`pr-N` with the same positive PR number; Production and rollback must pair
   182	`prod` with no PR number. Missing, empty, partial-number, unsafe-path and
   183	secret-bearing URL input fails with a value-free tagged error. Chromium is one
   184	focused host adapter acquired and closed through an Effect Scope, including on
   185	failure or interruption. Provider-free boundary tests prove those local input
   186	and cleanup rules only; they do not prove a hosted deployment. The harness
   187	writes candidate-qualified desktop/mobile PNGs and emits the behavioural
   188	observation used to build Schema-decoded receipts. The first dated
   189	Preview observation was torn down but did not meet the final evidence contract,
   190	so it remains disconfirming history. Fresh candidate `d9cb894…` passed the
   191	corrected hosted, screenshot and pre-mutation contracts, independent
   192	adversarial review and full repository gates and was then torn down; DCD-002
   193	is accepted. DCD-003 then deployed that source to fixed `prod`, qualified
   194	`c99984c…` through Preview and Production, removed the successor Preview, and
   195	restored `d9cb894…` through the same normal Alchemy graph. The current
   196	dated Production readback observed one stable Worker URL and restored
   197	source-bound state; it does not establish timeless availability. This does not
   198	claim byte promotion, recovery from known broken content, a custom domain/DNS
   199	route, a paid plan or release/publication.
   200	
   201	`check-import-boundaries` rejects server-only content, service, generated-source
   202	and runtime imports from browser-reachable app modules. The docs app has no
   203	browser Effect runtime. Its `.server.ts` loader module is the only route edge
   204	that acquires `DocsContentService`, and the module-scoped server runtime is
   205	reused for the server isolate. The same runtime owns a private live
   206	`DocsRuntimeProbe` Layer. That Layer acquires one Effect `Ref` construction
   207	state and an identifier produced by Effect `Random`; focused tests inject an
   208	exact deterministic identifier and dispose the complete runtime. The runtime
   209	factory exposes disposal so tests and future host lifecycle integration can
   210	release all Layers; the current hosting adapter does not provide an
   211	application shutdown hook.
   212	
   213	The Worker entry accepts the exact
   214	`x-taxkit-docs-runtime-proof: construction-count` opt-in header and returns a
   215	non-secret construction count plus random isolate identifier. The host callback
   216	runs the typed read through the application runtime and Schema-encodes it only
   217	at response-header egress; it owns no counter or randomness itself. This
   218	temporary deployment-migration channel proves reuse within the observed
   219	process/isolate across requests; it is not a public API and does not prove a
   220	singleton across Cloudflare isolates. Review it when the runtime, Worker entry,
   221	privacy boundary or proof channel changes. Retire it after an equally strong
   222	non-public provider oracle exists; otherwise retain its bounded
   223	one-identifier/two-header carrying cost explicitly through migration parity.
   224	
   225	The app-local MDX adapter classifies root-relative, query-only and authored
   226	relative `.mdx` destinations as TanStack routes while keeping external,
   227	protocol-relative, mail, download, repository-source and same-document
   228	destinations as anchors. It removes an authored `.mdx` suffix before any query
   229	or fragment without changing either suffix. Sidebar, home and MDX route links
   230	set one app-owned navigation-focus intent; the destination heading consumes it
   231	after a client transition. Initial hydration does not set that intent. The
   232	route container owns responsive navigation state and retry commands; render
   233	leaves receive readonly values and callbacks and do not acquire services or
   234	execute runtimes.
   235	
   236	## Authoring rules
   237	
   238	Before writing or reviewing public docs, read:
   239	
   240	- [Documentation style](../../docs/standards/documentation-style.md)
   241	- [Documentation writing](../../docs/standards/documentation-writing.md)
   242	- [Documentation templates](../../docs/standards/documentation-templates.md)
   243	- [Documentation review](../../docs/standards/documentation-review.md)
   244	- [Documentation architecture](../../docs/standards/documentation-architecture.md)
   245	- [Documentation user journeys](../../docs/standards/documentation-user-journeys.md)
   246	
   247	Use the matching template and user journey for each page. If a repeated page
   248	shape does not have a template, add the template before writing more pages in
   249	that shape.
   250	
   251	The required frontmatter `status` is schema-validated. `draft` means authored,
   252	locally renderable, visibly labelled candidate content, not accepted-current
   253	truth, publication, deployment, availability, accuracy, or user visibility.
   254	`published` means explicitly accepted current public documentation, still not
   255	runtime or external availability proof. Preserve draft pages unless explicit
   256	page-level acceptance records their transition. `bun run check:docs` enforces
   257	status representation and path ownership without asserting external state.
   258	
   259	## Validation graph
   260	
     1	---
     2	document_type: developer-guide
     3	lifecycle: current
     4	authority: supporting
     5	owner: taxkit-deployment-tool-owner
     6	last_reviewed: 2026-08-24
     7	review_trigger: docs deployment command, receipt Schema, workflow adapter, provider inventory, authority, or proof change
     8	---
     9	
    10	# Docs deployment tooling
    11	
    12	This directory owns repository-side validation, workflow receipt checks and
    13	provider/state inventory for the docs application. Durable resource policy
    14	lives in [`../../docs/architecture/deployment.md`](../../docs/architecture/deployment.md);
    15	operator procedure and authority live in
    16	[`../../docs/runbooks/docs-deployment.md`](../../docs/runbooks/docs-deployment.md).
    17	
    18	## Current boundaries
    19	
    20	- `schemas.ts`, `workflow-receipts.schemas.ts`, `workflow-check.schemas.ts` and
    21	  `inventory.schemas.ts` own current external representations and closed safe
    22	  errors. `schemas.ts` also decodes immutable historical v1/v2 receipts, while
    23	  current v2 plans admit only the native one-resource graph. Historical
    24	  decoders are not current deployment admission.
    25	- `input.boundary.ts` owns repository-relative retained-evidence reads.
    26	- `workflow-check.boundary.ts` owns workflow-provided file, JSON and SHA-256
    27	  ingress through Effect FileSystem, Crypto and Schema.
    28	- `inventory-credentials.boundary.ts` owns Alchemy state-store credential
    29	  ingress. It distinguishes absent, malformed and unreadable inputs, rejects
    30	  excess fields, keeps the bearer redacted and checks account identity before
    31	  state construction.
    32	- Each `workflow-*-check.runtime.ts` file decodes its Config Schema, calls the
    33	  shared boundary and one typed verification program, logs safe fields through
    34	  Effect Console, provides Bun services and executes once through
    35	  `BunRuntime.runMain`.
    36	- `workflow-evidence.schemas.ts`, `workflow-evidence.ts` and
    37	  `workflow-evidence.runtime.ts` form one closed command with `bootstrap`,
    38	  `plan`, `replan` and `provider` modes. It calculates shared tracked-file identities, reuses
    39	  the beta.64 plan projection and provider inventory Schemas, decodes bounded
    40	  Wrangler JSON, and encodes sanitised bootstrap, plan, provider and GitHub
    41	  output files. Its only child process is fixed `git ls-files`; it cannot choose
    42	  or run Alchemy, Wrangler, GitHub or another executable.
    43	- `inventory.runtime.ts` is the provider/state readback composition owner. It
    44	  remains read-only unless a separately authorized workflow owns mutation.
    45	- `strict-boundaries.policy.ts` checks the named application and deployment
    46	  adapters for ambient host access, raw concurrency, lost workflow/credential
    47	  boundaries and unmanaged docs runtime state.
    48	- Root `alchemy.run.ts` owns the native
    49	  `Cloudflare.Website.Vite("DocsWebsite")` resource. This directory does not
    50	  build or spawn the docs app.
    51	- `workflow-plan-projection.ts` is the single beta.64-bound host adapter for
    52	  Alchemy's text plan output. It admits only the current native Website
    53	  resource and fails closed on any other resource line. The
    54	  `fixtures/alchemy-beta.64/` manifest binds five real sanitised GitHub
    55	  artefact captures to Alchemy `2.0.0-beta.64`, upstream commit
    56	  `31edd3c4b2f0f3310fad07f5423aee20cf72be8d`, their source run/artefact
    57	  identities and SHA-256 digests. The fixture tests recompute every digest and
    58	  cover create, update, no-op, delete and already-absent destroy.
    59	
    60	The retired orphan classifier has no current workflow, command, Schema,
    61	service, runtime or child-process boundary. Its immutable JSON receipts remain
    62	historical evidence; they are not a contributor-lifecycle system.
    63	
    64	The one remaining Promise host bridge is `apps/docs/src/server.ts`: TanStack's
    65	Cloudflare `fetch` callback crosses into the app-owned `ManagedRuntime` through
    66	`runPromise`. This is a framework adapter, not domain execution ownership.
    67	
    68	## Local verification
    69	
    70	```sh
    71	bun run check:docs-deployment:types
    72	bun run check:docs-deployment-tools:types
    73	bun run test:docs-deployment
    74	bun run check:docs-deployment
    75	```
    76	
    77	The focused tests cover Config and receipt boundaries, every workflow-evidence
    78	mode, credential failures, account mismatch, plan/resource admission,
    79	workflow identity, deterministic output encoding, secret-negative failures,
    80	the version-bound real plan fixtures, historical receipt classification and
    81	static adapter contracts. Root
    82	`verification` invokes them once. These local commands do not dispatch
    83	workflows, access providers, deploy, destroy, prove hosted behavior or grant
    84	operational authority.

    11	
    12	# Alchemy deployment structure corrections
    13	
    14	## Status and admission
    15	
    16	Cooper accepted this whole SPEC, all four tasks and all eight finding
    17	dispositions on 2026-08-24. All four tasks are implemented. The
    18	[completed execution plan](../exec-plans/completed/alchemy-deployment-structure-corrections.md)
    19	records the ordered slices and [pull request #71](https://github.com/crcorbett/taxkit/pull/71)
    20	merged the verified candidate as
    21	`28ed00f884e74460c5b5efc3314f67c6457cf558` after hosted Quality run
    22	`32685832709` passed. Post-merge Quality run `32686064167` and
    23	receipt-reconciliation run `32686129314` passed on that exact merge.
    24	
    25	The accepted provider boundary permitted only the existing TaxKit docs Preview
    26	plan/bootstrap/state and provider readback needed for real beta.64 evidence.
    27	The implementation used existing retained GitHub artefacts and did not manually
    28	dispatch a provider workflow. Merging pull request #71 automatically ran the
    29	existing Preview teardown workflow for `pr-71`. Its mutation-capable bootstrap
    30	completed, two destroy dry-runs agreed on `Plan: no changes`, and provider/state
    31	readback confirmed that the stage and Worker were already absent, so the actual
    32	destroy was skipped. The bootstrap receipt cannot establish which of its
    33	allowed credential-refresh, secret-read or state-store effects occurred.
    34	Production deploy or rollback, DNS or custom-domain change, package
    35	publication, credential creation or rotation, broad Cloudflare cleanup and
    36	unrelated provider mutation remain outside authority. Every permitted provider
    37	operation still needs the exact principal, operation, resource, environment,
    38	rollback and readback required by the
    39	[authority model](../operations/authority-model.md).
    40	
    41	The sibling task ledger is
    42	[`alchemy-deployment-structure-corrections.tasks.json`](./alchemy-deployment-structure-corrections.tasks.json).
    43	The accepted audit register is
    44	[`accepted-findings.json`](../documentation-audit/alchemy-deployment-structure/accepted-findings.json).
    45	
    46	## Evidence baseline
    47	
    48	The audit and this recheck use the same current default-branch revision:
    49	`42230517ad96ab20a260fad3ce75b29421e59975`. On 2026-08-24,
    50	`origin/main` resolved to that revision, so none of the five confirmed findings
    51	was already fixed.
    52	
    53	The dependency baseline below comes from the repository package manifests, the
    54	exact resolutions in `bun.lock` and a successful `bun install
    55	--frozen-lockfile` on 2026-08-24. This proves local resolution only; it does not
    56	prove a hosted runner or provider dependency.
    57	
    58	| Boundary | Exact baseline |
    59	| --- | --- |
    60	| TaxKit | `42230517ad96ab20a260fad3ce75b29421e59975` |
    61	| Alchemy | `2.0.0-beta.64`; upstream tag `v2.0.0-beta.64`; commit `31edd3c4b2f0f3310fad07f5423aee20cf72be8d` |
    62	| Effect | `effect`, `@effect/platform-bun`, `@effect/platform-node` and `@effect/vitest` at `4.0.0-beta.100` |
    63	| Cloudflare integration | `@distilled.cloud/cloudflare` `0.30.1`; its Rolldown, runtime and Vite plugin packages at `0.13.8`; direct `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` `1.47.0`; Wrangler `4.114.0` |
    64	| Worker runtime | direct `workerd` `1.20260722.1`; Alchemy's nested runtime resolution `1.20260704.1` |
    65	| TanStack | `@tanstack/react-start` `1.167.65`; `@tanstack/react-router` `1.169.2` |
    66	| Fumadocs | `fumadocs-core` `16.9.3`; `fumadocs-mdx` `14.3.2` |
    67	
    68	The Alchemy source and official documentation establish these beta.64 facts:
    69	
    70	- `Cloudflare.StateStore.State.bootstrap` can resume a local deployment,
    71	  refresh cached credentials, upload a short-lived edge-preview Worker to read
    72	  the secret, and create or upgrade the state-store Worker.
    73	- the first `deploy`, `plan` or `dev` can therefore prepare or change state-store
    74	  resources before the requested operation continues;
    75	- `Cloudflare.Website.Vite` owns one Vite build and injects the Cloudflare Vite
    76	  plugin; and
    77	- Alchemy's CI guidance uses a non-cancellable deployment concurrency group.
    78	
    79	Primary upstream references:
    80	
    81	- [Alchemy beta.64 source](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/tree/v2.0.0-beta.64)
    82	- [State-store behaviour](https://alchemy.run/state-store/)
    83	- [Cloudflare Vite ownership](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/vite/)
    84	- [CI concurrency](https://alchemy.run/environments/ci/)
    85	
    86	## Problem
    87	
    88	The native deployment graph is sound, but five surrounding safety and truth
    89	contracts are not. A Production plan can cancel a Production mutation, secrets
    90	are available to unrelated workflow steps, bootstrap is described too narrowly,
    91	the hosted-proof input boundary is permissive, and the current runbook mixes
    92	retired and current operations.
    93	
    94	The audit also identified useful bounded work for duplicated workflow evidence,
    95	real beta.64 parser fixtures and manual CLI lock limits. Leaving those decisions
    96	implicit would make the implementation incomplete.
    97	
    98	## Goals
    99	
   100	1. Make Production plan, deploy and rollback mutually exclusive and
   101	   non-cancellable within the shared Production stage lock.
   102	2. Make the Cloudflare token available only to named provider steps.
   103	3. Describe and prove bootstrap as mutation-capable state preparation.
   104	4. Decode hosted-proof configuration once through Effect Config and Schema,
   105	   with safe typed failures and scoped browser cleanup.
   106	5. Give operators one current, one-resource `DocsWebsite` procedure.
   107	6. Replace repeated workflow evidence shell with one narrow typed Effect
   108	   command while YAML keeps authority and sequencing.
   109	7. Test the version-bound plan parser with sanitised real beta.64 output.
   110	8. State that GitHub workflow locks do not lock manual CLI mutation.
   111	
   112	## Non-goals
   113	
   114	- Do not add another Cloudflare resource, another build process or `DocsBuild`.
   115	- Do not replace `Cloudflare.Website.Vite("DocsWebsite")` or move its build
   116	  lifecycle out of Alchemy.
   117	- Do not create a generic infrastructure framework, shell runner, provider
   118	  client wrapper, `helpers`, `common` or `utils` layer.
   119	- Do not add a shared external lease. Manual mutation is not a supported normal
   120	  operating mode.

    12	# Alchemy deployment structure corrections
    13	
    14	## Status and admission
    15	
    16	Cooper accepted this whole SPEC, all four tasks and all eight finding
    17	dispositions on 2026-08-24. All four tasks are implemented. The
    18	[completed execution plan](../exec-plans/completed/alchemy-deployment-structure-corrections.md)
    19	records the ordered slices and [pull request #71](https://github.com/crcorbett/taxkit/pull/71)
    20	merged the verified candidate as
    21	`28ed00f884e74460c5b5efc3314f67c6457cf558` after hosted Quality run
    22	`32685832709` passed. Post-merge Quality run `32686064167` and
    23	receipt-reconciliation run `32686129314` passed on that exact merge.
    24	
    25	The accepted provider boundary permitted only the existing TaxKit docs Preview
    26	plan/bootstrap/state and provider readback needed for real beta.64 evidence.
    27	The implementation used existing retained GitHub artefacts and did not manually
    28	dispatch a provider workflow. Merging pull request #71 automatically ran the
    29	existing Preview teardown workflow for `pr-71`. Its mutation-capable bootstrap
    30	completed, two destroy dry-runs agreed on `Plan: no changes`, and provider/state
    31	readback confirmed that the stage and Worker were already absent, so the actual
    32	destroy was skipped. The bootstrap receipt cannot establish which of its
    33	allowed credential-refresh, secret-read or state-store effects occurred.
    34	Production deploy or rollback, DNS or custom-domain change, package
    35	publication, credential creation or rotation, broad Cloudflare cleanup and
    36	unrelated provider mutation remain outside authority. Every permitted provider
    37	operation still needs the exact principal, operation, resource, environment,
    38	rollback and readback required by the
    39	[authority model](../operations/authority-model.md).
    40	
    41	The sibling task ledger is
    42	[`alchemy-deployment-structure-corrections.tasks.json`](./alchemy-deployment-structure-corrections.tasks.json).
    43	The accepted audit register is
    44	[`accepted-findings.json`](../documentation-audit/alchemy-deployment-structure/accepted-findings.json).
    45	
    46	## Evidence baseline
    47	
    48	The audit and this recheck use the same current default-branch revision:
    49	`42230517ad96ab20a260fad3ce75b29421e59975`. On 2026-08-24,
    50	`origin/main` resolved to that revision, so none of the five confirmed findings
    51	was already fixed.
    52	
    53	The dependency baseline below comes from the repository package manifests, the
    54	exact resolutions in `bun.lock` and a successful `bun install
    55	--frozen-lockfile` on 2026-08-24. This proves local resolution only; it does not
    56	prove a hosted runner or provider dependency.
    57	
    58	| Boundary | Exact baseline |
    59	| --- | --- |
    60	| TaxKit | `42230517ad96ab20a260fad3ce75b29421e59975` |
    61	| Alchemy | `2.0.0-beta.64`; upstream tag `v2.0.0-beta.64`; commit `31edd3c4b2f0f3310fad07f5423aee20cf72be8d` |
    62	| Effect | `effect`, `@effect/platform-bun`, `@effect/platform-node` and `@effect/vitest` at `4.0.0-beta.100` |
    63	| Cloudflare integration | `@distilled.cloud/cloudflare` `0.30.1`; its Rolldown, runtime and Vite plugin packages at `0.13.8`; direct `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` `1.47.0`; Wrangler `4.114.0` |
    64	| Worker runtime | direct `workerd` `1.20260722.1`; Alchemy's nested runtime resolution `1.20260704.1` |
    65	| TanStack | `@tanstack/react-start` `1.167.65`; `@tanstack/react-router` `1.169.2` |
    66	| Fumadocs | `fumadocs-core` `16.9.3`; `fumadocs-mdx` `14.3.2` |
    67	
    68	The Alchemy source and official documentation establish these beta.64 facts:
    69	
    70	- `Cloudflare.StateStore.State.bootstrap` can resume a local deployment,
    71	  refresh cached credentials, upload a short-lived edge-preview Worker to read
    72	  the secret, and create or upgrade the state-store Worker.
    73	- the first `deploy`, `plan` or `dev` can therefore prepare or change state-store
    74	  resources before the requested operation continues;
    75	- `Cloudflare.Website.Vite` owns one Vite build and injects the Cloudflare Vite
    76	  plugin; and
    77	- Alchemy's CI guidance uses a non-cancellable deployment concurrency group.
    78	
    79	Primary upstream references:
    80	
    81	- [Alchemy beta.64 source](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/tree/v2.0.0-beta.64)
    82	- [State-store behaviour](https://alchemy.run/state-store/)
    83	- [Cloudflare Vite ownership](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/vite/)
    84	- [CI concurrency](https://alchemy.run/environments/ci/)
    85	
    86	## Problem
    87	
    88	The native deployment graph is sound, but five surrounding safety and truth
    89	contracts are not. A Production plan can cancel a Production mutation, secrets
    90	are available to unrelated workflow steps, bootstrap is described too narrowly,
    91	the hosted-proof input boundary is permissive, and the current runbook mixes
    92	retired and current operations.
    93	
    94	The audit also identified useful bounded work for duplicated workflow evidence,
    95	real beta.64 parser fixtures and manual CLI lock limits. Leaving those decisions
    96	implicit would make the implementation incomplete.
    97	
    98	## Goals
    99	
   100	1. Make Production plan, deploy and rollback mutually exclusive and
   101	   non-cancellable within the shared Production stage lock.
   102	2. Make the Cloudflare token available only to named provider steps.
   103	3. Describe and prove bootstrap as mutation-capable state preparation.
   104	4. Decode hosted-proof configuration once through Effect Config and Schema,
   105	   with safe typed failures and scoped browser cleanup.
   106	5. Give operators one current, one-resource `DocsWebsite` procedure.
   107	6. Replace repeated workflow evidence shell with one narrow typed Effect
   108	   command while YAML keeps authority and sequencing.
   109	7. Test the version-bound plan parser with sanitised real beta.64 output.
   110	8. State that GitHub workflow locks do not lock manual CLI mutation.
   111	
   112	## Non-goals
   113	
   114	- Do not add another Cloudflare resource, another build process or `DocsBuild`.
   115	- Do not replace `Cloudflare.Website.Vite("DocsWebsite")` or move its build
   116	  lifecycle out of Alchemy.
   117	- Do not create a generic infrastructure framework, shell runner, provider
   118	  client wrapper, `helpers`, `common` or `utils` layer.
   119	- Do not add a shared external lease. Manual mutation is not a supported normal
   120	  operating mode.

    12	# Alchemy deployment structure corrections
    13	
    14	## Status and admission
    15	
    16	Cooper accepted this whole SPEC, all four tasks and all eight finding
    17	dispositions on 2026-08-24. All four tasks are implemented. The
    18	[completed execution plan](../exec-plans/completed/alchemy-deployment-structure-corrections.md)
    19	records the ordered slices and [pull request #71](https://github.com/crcorbett/taxkit/pull/71)
    20	merged the verified candidate as
    21	`28ed00f884e74460c5b5efc3314f67c6457cf558` after hosted Quality run
    22	`32685832709` passed. Post-merge Quality run `32686064167` and
    23	receipt-reconciliation run `32686129314` passed on that exact merge.
    24	
    25	The accepted provider boundary permitted only the existing TaxKit docs Preview
    26	plan/bootstrap/state and provider readback needed for real beta.64 evidence.
    27	The implementation used existing retained GitHub artefacts and did not manually
    28	dispatch a provider workflow. Merging pull request #71 automatically ran the
    29	existing Preview teardown workflow for `pr-71`. Its mutation-capable bootstrap
    30	completed, two destroy dry-runs agreed on `Plan: no changes`, and provider/state
    31	readback confirmed that the stage and Worker were already absent, so the actual
    32	destroy was skipped. The bootstrap receipt cannot establish which of its
    33	allowed credential-refresh, secret-read or state-store effects occurred.
    34	Production deploy or rollback, DNS or custom-domain change, package
    35	publication, credential creation or rotation, broad Cloudflare cleanup and
    36	unrelated provider mutation remain outside authority. Every permitted provider
    37	operation still needs the exact principal, operation, resource, environment,
    38	rollback and readback required by the
    39	[authority model](../operations/authority-model.md).
    40

    42	[`alchemy-deployment-structure-corrections.tasks.json`](./alchemy-deployment-structure-corrections.tasks.json).
    43	The accepted audit register is
    44	[`accepted-findings.json`](../documentation-audit/alchemy-deployment-structure/accepted-findings.json).
    45	
    46	## Evidence baseline
    47	
    48	The audit and this recheck use the same current default-branch revision:
    49	`42230517ad96ab20a260fad3ce75b29421e59975`. On 2026-08-24,
    50	`origin/main` resolved to that revision, so none of the five confirmed findings
    51	was already fixed.
    52	
    53	The dependency baseline below comes from the repository package manifests, the
    54	exact resolutions in `bun.lock` and a successful `bun install
    55	--frozen-lockfile` on 2026-08-24. This proves local resolution only; it does not
    56	prove a hosted runner or provider dependency.
    57	
    58	| Boundary | Exact baseline |
    59	| --- | --- |
    60	| TaxKit | `42230517ad96ab20a260fad3ce75b29421e59975` |
    61	| Alchemy | `2.0.0-beta.64`; upstream tag `v2.0.0-beta.64`; commit `31edd3c4b2f0f3310fad07f5423aee20cf72be8d` |
    62	| Effect | `effect`, `@effect/platform-bun`, `@effect/platform-node` and `@effect/vitest` at `4.0.0-beta.100` |
    63	| Cloudflare integration | `@distilled.cloud/cloudflare` `0.30.1`; its Rolldown, runtime and Vite plugin packages at `0.13.8`; direct `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` `1.47.0`; Wrangler `4.114.0` |
    64	| Worker runtime | direct `workerd` `1.20260722.1`; Alchemy's nested runtime resolution `1.20260704.1` |
    65	| TanStack | `@tanstack/react-start` `1.167.65`; `@tanstack/react-router` `1.169.2` |
    66	| Fumadocs | `fumadocs-core` `16.9.3`; `fumadocs-mdx` `14.3.2` |
    67	
    68	The Alchemy source and official documentation establish these beta.64 facts:
    69	
    70	- `Cloudflare.StateStore.State.bootstrap` can resume a local deployment,
    71	  refresh cached credentials, upload a short-lived edge-preview Worker to read
    72	  the secret, and create or upgrade the state-store Worker.
    73	- the first `deploy`, `plan` or `dev` can therefore prepare or change state-store
    74	  resources before the requested operation continues;
    75	- `Cloudflare.Website.Vite` owns one Vite build and injects the Cloudflare Vite
    76	  plugin; and
    77	- Alchemy's CI guidance uses a non-cancellable deployment concurrency group.
    78	
    79	Primary upstream references:
    80	
    81	- [Alchemy beta.64 source](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/tree/v2.0.0-beta.64)
    82	- [State-store behaviour](https://alchemy.run/state-store/)
    83	- [Cloudflare Vite ownership](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/vite/)
    84	- [CI concurrency](https://alchemy.run/environments/ci/)
    85	
    86	## Problem
    87	
    88	The native deployment graph is sound, but five surrounding safety and truth
    89	contracts are not. A Production plan can cancel a Production mutation, secrets
    90	are available to unrelated workflow steps, bootstrap is described too narrowly,
    91	the hosted-proof input boundary is permissive, and the current runbook mixes
    92	retired and current operations.
    93	
    94	The audit also identified useful bounded work for duplicated workflow evidence,
    95	real beta.64 parser fixtures and manual CLI lock limits. Leaving those decisions
    96	implicit would make the implementation incomplete.
    97	
    98	## Goals
    99	
   100	1. Make Production plan, deploy and rollback mutually exclusive and
   101	   non-cancellable within the shared Production stage lock.
   102	2. Make the Cloudflare token available only to named provider steps.
   103	3. Describe and prove bootstrap as mutation-capable state preparation.
   104	4. Decode hosted-proof configuration once through Effect Config and Schema,
   105	   with safe typed failures and scoped browser cleanup.
   106	5. Give operators one current, one-resource `DocsWebsite` procedure.
   107	6. Replace repeated workflow evidence shell with one narrow typed Effect
   108	   command while YAML keeps authority and sequencing.
   109	7. Test the version-bound plan parser with sanitised real beta.64 output.
   110	8. State that GitHub workflow locks do not lock manual CLI mutation.
   111	
   112	## Non-goals
   113	
   114	- Do not add another Cloudflare resource, another build process or `DocsBuild`.
   115	- Do not replace `Cloudflare.Website.Vite("DocsWebsite")` or move its build
   116	  lifecycle out of Alchemy.
   117	- Do not create a generic infrastructure framework, shell runner, provider
   118	  client wrapper, `helpers`, `common` or `utils` layer.
   119	- Do not add a shared external lease. Manual mutation is not a supported normal
   120	  operating mode.

    12	# Alchemy deployment structure corrections
    13	
    14	## Status and admission
    15	
    16	Cooper accepted this whole SPEC, all four tasks and all eight finding
    17	dispositions on 2026-08-24. All four tasks are implemented. The
    18	[completed execution plan](../exec-plans/completed/alchemy-deployment-structure-corrections.md)
    19	records the ordered slices and [pull request #71](https://github.com/crcorbett/taxkit/pull/71)
    20	merged the verified candidate as
    21	`28ed00f884e74460c5b5efc3314f67c6457cf558` after hosted Quality run
    22	`32685832709` passed. Post-merge Quality run `32686064167` and
    23	receipt-reconciliation run `32686129314` passed on that exact merge.
    24	
    25	The accepted provider boundary permitted only the existing TaxKit docs Preview
    26	plan/bootstrap/state and provider readback needed for real beta.64 evidence.
    27	The implementation used existing retained GitHub artefacts and did not manually
    28	dispatch a provider workflow. Merging pull request #71 automatically ran the
    29	existing Preview teardown workflow for `pr-71`. Its mutation-capable bootstrap
    30	completed, two destroy dry-runs agreed on `Plan: no changes`, and provider/state
    31	readback confirmed that the stage and Worker were already absent, so the actual
    32	destroy was skipped. The bootstrap receipt cannot establish which of its
    33	allowed credential-refresh, secret-read or state-store effects occurred.
    34	Production deploy or rollback, DNS or custom-domain change, package
    35	publication, credential creation or rotation, broad Cloudflare cleanup and
    36	unrelated provider mutation remain outside authority. Every permitted provider
    37	operation still needs the exact principal, operation, resource, environment,
    38	rollback and readback required by the
    39	[authority model](../operations/authority-model.md).
    40	
    41	The sibling task ledger is
    42	[`alchemy-deployment-structure-corrections.tasks.json`](./alchemy-deployment-structure-corrections.tasks.json).
    43	The accepted audit register is
    44	[`accepted-findings.json`](../documentation-audit/alchemy-deployment-structure/accepted-findings.json).
    45	
    46	## Evidence baseline
    47	
    48	The audit and this recheck use the same current default-branch revision:
    49	`42230517ad96ab20a260fad3ce75b29421e59975`. On 2026-08-24,
    50	`origin/main` resolved to that revision, so none of the five confirmed findings
    51	was already fixed.
    52	
    53	The dependency baseline below comes from the repository package manifests, the
    54	exact resolutions in `bun.lock` and a successful `bun install
    55	--frozen-lockfile` on 2026-08-24. This proves local resolution only; it does not
    56	prove a hosted runner or provider dependency.
    57	
    58	| Boundary | Exact baseline |
    59	| --- | --- |
    60	| TaxKit | `42230517ad96ab20a260fad3ce75b29421e59975` |
    61	| Alchemy | `2.0.0-beta.64`; upstream tag `v2.0.0-beta.64`; commit `31edd3c4b2f0f3310fad07f5423aee20cf72be8d` |
    62	| Effect | `effect`, `@effect/platform-bun`, `@effect/platform-node` and `@effect/vitest` at `4.0.0-beta.100` |
    63	| Cloudflare integration | `@distilled.cloud/cloudflare` `0.30.1`; its Rolldown, runtime and Vite plugin packages at `0.13.8`; direct `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` `1.47.0`; Wrangler `4.114.0` |
    64	| Worker runtime | direct `workerd` `1.20260722.1`; Alchemy's nested runtime resolution `1.20260704.1` |
    65	| TanStack | `@tanstack/react-start` `1.167.65`; `@tanstack/react-router` `1.169.2` |
    66	| Fumadocs | `fumadocs-core` `16.9.3`; `fumadocs-mdx` `14.3.2` |
    67	
    68	The Alchemy source and official documentation establish these beta.64 facts:
    69	
    70	- `Cloudflare.StateStore.State.bootstrap` can resume a local deployment,
    71	  refresh cached credentials, upload a short-lived edge-preview Worker to read
    72	  the secret, and create or upgrade the state-store Worker.
    73	- the first `deploy`, `plan` or `dev` can therefore prepare or change state-store
    74	  resources before the requested operation continues;
    75	- `Cloudflare.Website.Vite` owns one Vite build and injects the Cloudflare Vite
    76	  plugin; and
    77	- Alchemy's CI guidance uses a non-cancellable deployment concurrency group.
    78	
    79	Primary upstream references:
    80	
    81	- [Alchemy beta.64 source](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/tree/v2.0.0-beta.64)
    82	- [State-store behaviour](https://alchemy.run/state-store/)
    83	- [Cloudflare Vite ownership](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/vite/)
    84	- [CI concurrency](https://alchemy.run/environments/ci/)
    85	
    86	## Problem
    87	
    88	The native deployment graph is sound, but five surrounding safety and truth
    89	contracts are not. A Production plan can cancel a Production mutation, secrets
    90	are available to unrelated workflow steps, bootstrap is described too narrowly,
    91	the hosted-proof input boundary is permissive, and the current runbook mixes
    92	retired and current operations.
    93	
    94	The audit also identified useful bounded work for duplicated workflow evidence,
    95	real beta.64 parser fixtures and manual CLI lock limits. Leaving those decisions
    96	implicit would make the implementation incomplete.
    97	
    98	## Goals
    99	
   100	1. Make Production plan, deploy and rollback mutually exclusive and
   101	   non-cancellable within the shared Production stage lock.
   102	2. Make the Cloudflare token available only to named provider steps.
   103	3. Describe and prove bootstrap as mutation-capable state preparation.
   104	4. Decode hosted-proof configuration once through Effect Config and Schema,
   105	   with safe typed failures and scoped browser cleanup.
   106	5. Give operators one current, one-resource `DocsWebsite` procedure.
   107	6. Replace repeated workflow evidence shell with one narrow typed Effect
   108	   command while YAML keeps authority and sequencing.
   109	7. Test the version-bound plan parser with sanitised real beta.64 output.
   110	8. State that GitHub workflow locks do not lock manual CLI mutation.
   111	
   112	## Non-goals
   113	
   114	- Do not add another Cloudflare resource, another build process or `DocsBuild`.
   115	- Do not replace `Cloudflare.Website.Vite("DocsWebsite")` or move its build
   116	  lifecycle out of Alchemy.
   117	- Do not create a generic infrastructure framework, shell runner, provider
   118	  client wrapper, `helpers`, `common` or `utils` layer.
   119	- Do not add a shared external lease. Manual mutation is not a supported normal
   120	  operating mode.

    10	# TaxKit operational authority
    11	
    12	Capability is not authority. Repository access or a runnable command does not
    13	identify the principal permitted to perform a consequential operation. Each
    14	run must bind identity, operation, resource, environment, approval boundary,
    15	duration or revocation, audit receipt, rollback precondition, and escalation.
    16	
    17	The repository carries no standing authority for the operations below. Their
    18	principal is `unknown`, so their status is `unknown-stop`:
    19	
    20	| Operation | Principal | Status | Required authority receipt |
    21	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
    22	| `versioning` | `unknown` | `unknown-stop` | Named principal; exact package/version train; local checkout; approval scope and duration; before/after manifest receipt; identified revert target. |
    23	| `commit` | `unknown` | `unknown-stop` | Named principal; exact paths, branch and message; approval duration; commit/tree readback; accepted semantic scope and revert owner. |
    24	| `push` | `unknown` | `unknown-stop` | Named principal; remote, branch and expected commit; approval duration; remote SHA readback; prior remote state and recovery authority. |
    25	| `tag` | `unknown` | `unknown-stop` | Named principal; provider, commit and immutable tag; approval duration; provider readback; provider-specific recovery. |
    26	| `release` | `unknown` | `unknown-stop` | Named principal; provider, target commit and hosted release identity; approval duration; release readback; provider-specific recovery. |
    27	| `registry-publication` | `unknown` | `unknown-stop` | Named principal; registry and exact package/version set; credential expiry/revocation; registry readback; deprecation/recovery plan. |
    28	| `deployment` | `unknown` | `unknown-stop` | Named principal; provider-specific app/infrastructure target; environment and duration; provider/runtime readback; tested rollback and reconciliation. |

    32	Read-only local diagnosis and static validation may proceed within the user's

    77	## Commands
    78	
    79	```sh
    80	bun install
    81	bun run --filter=api dev
    82	bun run --filter=web dev
    83	bun run --filter=docs dev
    84	bun run --filter=docs test:cloudflare-built
    85	bun run check:repository-paths
    86	bun run check:harness-governance
    87	bun run check:docs
    88	bun run knip:production
    89	bun run verification
    90	bun run test:skills
    91	bun run release:check

    93	bun run version-repo
    94	```
    95	
    96	`bun run --filter=api dev` serves the API through portless at
    97	`https://api.taxkit.localhost`. `bun run --filter=web dev` injects that
    98	portless URL into `TAXKIT_API_BASE_URL` and `VITE_TAXKIT_API_BASE_URL` before
    99	serving the web app at `https://taxkit.localhost`. `bun run --filter=docs dev`
   100	serves the public docs app at `https://docs.taxkit.localhost`. `bun run
   101	--filter=docs test:cloudflare-built` builds the exact Cloudflare target and
   102	exercises an isolated copy of its Worker/assets under local workerd; it does
   103	not access provider credentials or prove a deployment. `bun run
   104	check:repository-paths` rejects machine-local checkout references in tracked
   105	readable text without printing the matched private value. `bun run check:docs`
   106	checks maintainer metadata, links, documented commands, workspace README
   107	coverage, public/maintainer path separation, and generated-source ownership.
   108	It treats public content status as opaque and does not establish publication,
   109	availability, accuracy, or accepted-current truth. `bun run
   110	check:harness-governance` validates the repository-local harness profile,
   111	accepted HE crosswalk, skill-tree receipt, allowed overlays, relative Claude
   112	links, local skill references, critical journeys, and external non-claims. It
   113	does not read a global skill installation or establish remote Git, hosted CI,
   114	registry, release, deployment, provider, public-site, or external-consumer
   115	state. `bun run knip:production`
   116	checks the release-artifact package, repository command and
   117	API runtime graph without test or development reachability. `bun run
   118	verification` is the baseline verification command for documentation, package
   119	wiring and scaffold changes and includes repo-owned skill policy checks. `bun
   120	run test:skills` runs that focused stale-pattern suite directly. `bun run
   121	release:check` runs the complete ordered
   122	release evidence, including tests, builds, package artifacts, API smoke, docs
   123	browser proof and Changeset status.
   124	
   125	Deterministic repository commands run through Turbo, including the root
   126	validators used by `verification` and the app/package checks used by
   127	`release:check`. Token-bearing GitHub Quality runs may read and write Vercel
   128	Remote Cache on same-repository pull requests and `main`; fork pull requests
   129	receive no token and run the same full command graph locally. A missing token
   130	or cache service also falls back locally. Local remote-cache use is an explicit
   131	developer choice through `TURBO_TOKEN` and `TURBO_TEAM`. Never commit either
   132	credential or treat a cache hit as test, release, deployment or public
   133	availability proof.
   134	
   135	Quality also keeps separate GitHub caches for Bun package downloads and the
   136	Playwright Chromium binary. It does not cache `node_modules`: current warm
   137	hosted evidence shows the frozen Bun install takes only 1–2 seconds after the
   138	package cache restores, while the installed tree is about 1.4 GB. The workflow
   139	still runs frozen install plus Playwright system-dependency setup on every run.
   140	Keys use platform and dependency content, so pull requests may restore a
   141	matching cache saved by `main`. GitHub keeps pull-request writes on the
   142	pull-request merge ref, away from `main` and sibling pull requests. A miss or
   143	cache outage only changes download time.
   144	
   145	The trusted docs Preview, Production, teardown and receipt workflows use the
   146	same remote task cache for deterministic Turbo work. They use the same
   147	content-addressed Bun download keys, and browser workflows use the same
   148	content-addressed Chromium keys. GitHub ref scope controls writes. Exact
   149	candidate checks, provider plans or mutations, hosted readback and receipt
   150	promotion are always live and cannot be satisfied by a cache hit.

   111	accepted HE crosswalk, skill-tree receipt, allowed overlays, relative Claude

   121	release:check` runs the complete ordered

   142	pull-request merge ref, away from `main` and sibling pull requests. A miss or

    63	## Planned package families
    64	
    65	The architecture docs describe the intended package families for the tax engine:
    66	core primitives and facts, domain models, rule packs, API clients, SDKs, docs
    67	tooling and supporting app shells. Treat those as planned architecture unless a

    76	
    77	## Commands
    78	
    79	```sh
    80	bun install
    81	bun run --filter=api dev
    82	bun run --filter=web dev
    83	bun run --filter=docs dev
    84	bun run --filter=docs test:cloudflare-built
    85	bun run check:repository-paths
    86	bun run check:harness-governance
    87	bun run check:docs
    88	bun run knip:production
    89	bun run verification
    90	bun run test:skills
    91	bun run release:check
    92	bun run changeset
    93	bun run version-repo
    94	```
    95	
    96	`bun run --filter=api dev` serves the API through portless at
    97	`https://api.taxkit.localhost`. `bun run --filter=web dev` injects that
    98	portless URL into `TAXKIT_API_BASE_URL` and `VITE_TAXKIT_API_BASE_URL` before
    99	serving the web app at `https://taxkit.localhost`. `bun run --filter=docs dev`
   100	serves the public docs app at `https://docs.taxkit.localhost`. `bun run
   101	--filter=docs test:cloudflare-built` builds the exact Cloudflare target and
   102	exercises an isolated copy of its Worker/assets under local workerd; it does
   103	not access provider credentials or prove a deployment. `bun run
   104	check:repository-paths` rejects machine-local checkout references in tracked
   105	readable text without printing the matched private value. `bun run check:docs`
   106	checks maintainer metadata, links, documented commands, workspace README
   107	coverage, public/maintainer path separation, and generated-source ownership.
   108	It treats public content status as opaque and does not establish publication,
   109	availability, accuracy, or accepted-current truth. `bun run
   110	check:harness-governance` validates the repository-local harness profile,
   111	accepted HE crosswalk, skill-tree receipt, allowed overlays, relative Claude
   112	links, local skill references, critical journeys, and external non-claims. It
   113	does not read a global skill installation or establish remote Git, hosted CI,
   114	registry, release, deployment, provider, public-site, or external-consumer
   115	state. `bun run knip:production`
   116	checks the release-artifact package, repository command and
   117	API runtime graph without test or development reachability. `bun run
   118	verification` is the baseline verification command for documentation, package
   119	wiring and scaffold changes and includes repo-owned skill policy checks. `bun
   120	run test:skills` runs that focused stale-pattern suite directly. `bun run
   121	release:check` runs the complete ordered
   122	release evidence, including tests, builds, package artifacts, API smoke, docs
   123	browser proof and Changeset status.
   124	
   125	Deterministic repository commands run through Turbo, including the root
   126	validators used by `verification` and the app/package checks used by
   127	`release:check`. Token-bearing GitHub Quality runs may read and write Vercel
   128	Remote Cache on same-repository pull requests and `main`; fork pull requests
   129	receive no token and run the same full command graph locally. A missing token
   130	or cache service also falls back locally. Local remote-cache use is an explicit
   131	developer choice through `TURBO_TOKEN` and `TURBO_TEAM`. Never commit either
   132	credential or treat a cache hit as test, release, deployment or public
   133	availability proof.
   134	
   135	Quality also keeps separate GitHub caches for Bun package downloads and the
   136	Playwright Chromium binary. It does not cache `node_modules`: current warm
   137	hosted evidence shows the frozen Bun install takes only 1–2 seconds after the
   138	package cache restores, while the installed tree is about 1.4 GB. The workflow
   139	still runs frozen install plus Playwright system-dependency setup on every run.
   140	Keys use platform and dependency content, so pull requests may restore a
   141	matching cache saved by `main`. GitHub keeps pull-request writes on the
   142	pull-request merge ref, away from `main` and sibling pull requests. A miss or
   143	cache outage only changes download time.
   144	
   145	The trusted docs Preview, Production, teardown and receipt workflows use the
   146	same remote task cache for deterministic Turbo work. They use the same
   147	content-addressed Bun download keys, and browser workflows use the same
   148	content-addressed Chromium keys. GitHub ref scope controls writes. Exact
   149	candidate checks, provider plans or mutations, hosted readback and receipt
   150	promotion are always live and cannot be satisfied by a cache hit.

   262	The secure provider connection now resolves account-owned permission groups and

     8	# API App
     9	
    10	Standalone Bun process for the TaxKit Effect HTTP API.
    11	
    12	## Scope
    13	
    14	`apps/api` owns process config, Bun server startup, request dispatch to
    15	`@taxkit/api-http/server` and graceful shutdown. API contracts, handlers,
    16	schemas, generated OpenAPI and docs routes stay in `packages/api/http`.
    17	
    18	## Runtime Shape
    19	
    20	The process entrypoint is an Effect program run with
    21	`@effect/platform-bun/BunRuntime.runMain`. Startup reads `ApiServerConfig` from
    22	`ApiAppLayer`, requests are served by the Bun-backed `HttpServer` layer, and
    23	`SIGINT` or `SIGTERM` interrupts the root Effect fiber so scoped finalizers stop
    24	the Bun server.
    25	
    26	Local defaults:
    27	
    28	- host: `127.0.0.1`
    29	- port: `4000`
    30	
    31	Environment overrides:
    32	
    33	- `API_HOST`
    34	- `API_PORT`
    35	- `PORT` as the fallback port supplied by portless
    36	
    37	## Routes
    38	
    39	- `GET /api/health`
    40	- `GET /api/docs`
    41	- `GET /api/docs/openapi.json`
    42	- `GET /api/v1/jurisdictions`
    43	- `GET /api/v1/tax-years`
    44	- `GET /api/v1/calculators`
    45	- `GET /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId`
    46	- `GET /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId/schema`
    47	- `POST /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId/calculate`
    48	- `GET /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId/graph`
    49	- `GET /api/v1/facts`
    50	- `GET /api/v1/rules`
    51	
    52	Public calculation routes are calculator, fact, rule and graph driven.
    53	Jurisdiction and tax year are calculator context, not top-level route families.
    54	The initial calculator IDs are `au.pay.take-home`, `au.pay.withholdings` and
    55	`au.income-tax.annual`.
    56	
    57	Calculate payloads use canonical schema values from the rule packages. The
    58	generated OpenAPI request body shows supported fact shapes under `facts.anyOf`;
    59	for example, take-home-pay JSON includes tagged `GrossPay` and `Money` values.
    60	The calculator service validates facts again against the selected calculator,
    61	so annual-tax facts sent to `au.pay.take-home` return pay-calculator input help
    62	instead of being treated as a valid take-home request.
    63	
    64	## Changelog
    65	
    66	Public API contract and deployment-facing changes are tracked in
    67	[CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md). Package-level API contract changes are also
    68	tracked in [`@taxkit/api-http`](../../packages/api/http/CHANGELOG.md) through
    69	Changesets.

    77	bun run --filter=api check-types
    78	bun run --filter=api build

    88	
    89	`bun run --filter=api dev` serves this app through portless at

    91	into `TAXKIT_API_BASE_URL` for SSR and `VITE_TAXKIT_API_BASE_URL` for browser
    92	navigation.

     8	# API App
     9	
    10	Standalone Bun process for the TaxKit Effect HTTP API.
    11	
    12	## Scope
    13	
    14	`apps/api` owns process config, Bun server startup, request dispatch to
    15	`@taxkit/api-http/server` and graceful shutdown. API contracts, handlers,
    16	schemas, generated OpenAPI and docs routes stay in `packages/api/http`.
    17	
    18	## Runtime Shape
    19	
    20	The process entrypoint is an Effect program run with
    21	`@effect/platform-bun/BunRuntime.runMain`. Startup reads `ApiServerConfig` from
    22	`ApiAppLayer`, requests are served by the Bun-backed `HttpServer` layer, and
    23	`SIGINT` or `SIGTERM` interrupts the root Effect fiber so scoped finalizers stop
    24	the Bun server.
    25	
    26	Local defaults:
    27	
    28	- host: `127.0.0.1`
    29	- port: `4000`
    30	
    31	Environment overrides:
    32	
    33	- `API_HOST`
    34	- `API_PORT`
    35	- `PORT` as the fallback port supplied by portless
    36	
    37	## Routes
    38	
    39	- `GET /api/health`
    40	- `GET /api/docs`
    41	- `GET /api/docs/openapi.json`
    42	- `GET /api/v1/jurisdictions`
    43	- `GET /api/v1/tax-years`
    44	- `GET /api/v1/calculators`
    45	- `GET /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId`
    46	- `GET /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId/schema`
    47	- `POST /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId/calculate`
    48	- `GET /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId/graph`
    49	- `GET /api/v1/facts`
    50	- `GET /api/v1/rules`
    51	
    52	Public calculation routes are calculator, fact, rule and graph driven.
    53	Jurisdiction and tax year are calculator context, not top-level route families.
    54	The initial calculator IDs are `au.pay.take-home`, `au.pay.withholdings` and
    55	`au.income-tax.annual`.
    56	
    57	Calculate payloads use canonical schema values from the rule packages. The
    58	generated OpenAPI request body shows supported fact shapes under `facts.anyOf`;
    59	for example, take-home-pay JSON includes tagged `GrossPay` and `Money` values.
    60	The calculator service validates facts again against the selected calculator,
    61	so annual-tax facts sent to `au.pay.take-home` return pay-calculator input help
    62	instead of being treated as a valid take-home request.
    63

    11

    13

    22	`ApiAppLayer`, requests are served by the Bun-backed `HttpServer` layer, and

    38	
    39	- `GET /api/health`

    44	- `GET /api/v1/calculators`

    52	Public calculation routes are calculator, fact, rule and graph driven.
    53	Jurisdiction and tax year are calculator context, not top-level route families.

    26	
    27	## Runtime Shape
    28	
    29	The root route loads `@taxkit/api-http/client` through the route runtime and
    30	renders API health status from the standalone API service over HTTP.
    31	Server-only API exports must stay out of browser code.
    32	
    33	The web runtime reads the API origin from:
    34	
    35	- `TAXKIT_API_BASE_URL` on the server
    36	- `VITE_TAXKIT_API_BASE_URL` in the browser
    37	
    38	Both are required runtime config values and are validated with Effect Config and
    39	Effect Schema. `bun run --filter=web dev` injects both from
    40	`portless get api.taxkit`. Do not include `/api` in the base URL; the typed
    41	API client owns route prefixes.
    42	
    43	## Guardrails
    44	
    45	- Keep tax rules, facts and calculators in engine packages.
    46	- Use browser-safe API client exports from routes.
    47	- Do not import `@taxkit/api-http/server` from browser code.
    48	- Keep route data acquisition and trust-boundary conversion route-high. Render
    49	  the page shell and semantic landmarks before passing focused readonly values
    50	  and callbacks to leaves.
    51	- Keep local UI commands in leaves; keep remote or domain commands in the route
    52	  action or nearest policy-owning container.
    53	- Put loading, empty and recoverable error UI at the smallest owning boundary
    54	  while preserving a stable footprint and the surrounding page shell.
    55	- Keep the app README local; route durable architecture to `docs/architecture`.
    56	
    57	## Commands
    58	
    59	```bash
    60	bun run --filter=api dev
    61	bun run --filter=web dev
    62	bun run --filter=web check-types
    63	bun run --filter=web build
    64	```
    65	
    66	Run `apps/api` before loading the web root locally. Without the API process,
    67	the root route should fail with an attributable HTTP transport error rather
    68	than silently falling back to an in-process API.
    69	
    70	Use the portless URLs for local browser and app-to-app checks:
    71	
    72	- API: `https://api.taxkit.localhost`
    73	- Web: `https://taxkit.localhost`
    74	
    75	## Related Docs
    76	
    77	- `docs/architecture/frontend.md`
    78	- `docs/architecture/api-and-sdk.md`
    79	- `docs/architecture/deployment.md`
    80	- `docs/design-docs/abstraction-admission.md`

     6	---
     7	
     8	# API App
     9	
    10	Standalone Bun process for the TaxKit Effect HTTP API.
    11	
    12	## Scope
    13	
    14	`apps/api` owns process config, Bun server startup, request dispatch to
    15	`@taxkit/api-http/server` and graceful shutdown. API contracts, handlers,
    16	schemas, generated OpenAPI and docs routes stay in `packages/api/http`.
    17	
    18	## Runtime Shape
    19	
    20	The process entrypoint is an Effect program run with
    21	`@effect/platform-bun/BunRuntime.runMain`. Startup reads `ApiServerConfig` from
    22	`ApiAppLayer`, requests are served by the Bun-backed `HttpServer` layer, and
    23	`SIGINT` or `SIGTERM` interrupts the root Effect fiber so scoped finalizers stop
    24	the Bun server.
    25	
    26	Local defaults:
    27	
    28	- host: `127.0.0.1`
    29	- port: `4000`
    30	
    31	Environment overrides:
    32	
    33	- `API_HOST`
    34	- `API_PORT`
    35	- `PORT` as the fallback port supplied by portless
    36	
    37	## Routes
    38	
    39	- `GET /api/health`
    40	- `GET /api/docs`
    41	- `GET /api/docs/openapi.json`
    42	- `GET /api/v1/jurisdictions`
    43	- `GET /api/v1/tax-years`
    44	- `GET /api/v1/calculators`
    45	- `GET /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId`
    46	- `GET /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId/schema`
    47	- `POST /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId/calculate`
    48	- `GET /api/v1/calculators/:calculatorId/graph`
    49	- `GET /api/v1/facts`
    50	- `GET /api/v1/rules`
    51	
    52	Public calculation routes are calculator, fact, rule and graph driven.
    53	Jurisdiction and tax year are calculator context, not top-level route families.
    54	The initial calculator IDs are `au.pay.take-home`, `au.pay.withholdings` and
    55	`au.income-tax.annual`.
    56	
    57	Calculate payloads use canonical schema values from the rule packages. The
    58	generated OpenAPI request body shows supported fact shapes under `facts.anyOf`;
    59	for example, take-home-pay JSON includes tagged `GrossPay` and `Money` values.
    60	The calculator service validates facts again against the selected calculator,
    61	so annual-tax facts sent to `au.pay.take-home` return pay-calculator input help
    62	instead of being treated as a valid take-home request.
    63	
    64	## Changelog
    65	
    66	Public API contract and deployment-facing changes are tracked in
    67	[CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md). Package-level API contract changes are also
    68	tracked in [`@taxkit/api-http`](../../packages/api/http/CHANGELOG.md) through
    69	Changesets.
    70	
    71	## Commands
    72	
    73	```sh
    74	bun run --filter=api dev
    75	bun run --filter=api start
    76	bun run --filter=api smoke:public-routes
    77	bun run --filter=api check-types
    78	bun run --filter=api build
    79	bun run --filter=api clean
    80	```
    81	
    82	For local UI development, run the API and web app in separate terminals:
    83	
    84	```sh
    85	bun run --filter=api dev
    86	bun run --filter=web dev
    87	```
    88	
    89	`bun run --filter=api dev` serves this app through portless at
    90	`https://api.taxkit.localhost`. `bun run --filter=web dev` injects that URL
    91	into `TAXKIT_API_BASE_URL` for SSR and `VITE_TAXKIT_API_BASE_URL` for browser
    92	navigation.
    93	
    94	## Public-route smoke
    95	
    96	Use the app-owned smoke command when you need proof that the standalone Bun
    97	process serves the current public API contract:
    98	
    99	```sh
   100	bun run --filter=api smoke:public-routes
   101	```
   102	
   103	The command starts `apps/api` at `http://127.0.0.1:4173` by default, waits for
   104	`GET /api/health`, calls the public calculator metadata route, posts one
   105	take-home-pay calculation and reads the generated OpenAPI document. It then
   106	creates a temp consumer workspace outside the repo, writes a dependency-free
   107	`fetch` consumer and runs that consumer from the temp workspace against the
   108	same public HTTP routes:
   109	
   110	- `GET /api/health`
   111	- `GET /api/v1/calculators`
   112	- `POST /api/v1/calculators/au.pay.take-home/calculate`
   113	- `GET /api/docs/openapi.json`
   114	
   115	The smoke script owns process lifecycle only. It validates response bodies with
   116	schemas exported by `@taxkit/api-http` where those schemas are public, and it
   117	lets the app process stop through Effect-scoped child process cleanup on
   118	success or failure. The external consumer checks minimal public JSON evidence;
   119	canonical route schema validation stays in this repo-owned smoke script. The
   120	temp workspace is removed on success and failure.
   121	
   122	When the default loopback port is occupied, set `TAXKIT_API_SMOKE_PORT` to an
   123	available port. The isolated release-boundary harness uses this override so a
   124	neighbouring local development server cannot change its failure oracle.
   125	
   126	Use the failure simulation when you need deterministic cleanup evidence for a
   127	downstream consumer failure:
   128	
   129	```sh
   130	bun run --filter=api smoke:public-routes -- --simulate-downstream-failure
   131	```
   132	
   133	The simulation exits nonzero after the external consumer has covered the
   134	public routes, then removes the temp workspace and stops the API process.
   135	
   136	Use the portless URL for local API smoke checks:
   137	
   138	```sh
   139	curl https://api.taxkit.localhost/api/health
   140	curl https://api.taxkit.localhost/api/v1/calculators
